Mohammad Ullah J : On an application under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, this Court issued the Rule in the following terms: "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and decree dated 18-9-2016 (decree signed on 22-9-2016) passed by the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Appeal Tribunal, the respondent No. 1, in Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Appeal No. 92 of 2016 dismissing the appeal and thereby affirming the judgment and decree dated 10-3-2016 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet the respondent No. 2 in Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Case No. 541 of 2012 (impugned Annexures-I and I-1) releasing the property involved in the case in favour of respondent Nos. 5 to 8 in violation of the provisions of section 17(Gha) of the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Ain, 2001 should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper."

2. Pending hearing of the Rule, the operation of the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-9-2016 and 10-3-2016 were stayed initially for a period of 3 (three) months and from time to time the period of stay was extended.

3. The petitioner by filing an application also prayed for setting aside the judgment and decree dated 19-11-2015 passed by the respondent No. 2, Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No.3, Sylhet in Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 and for a direction upon the respondent No.2 to hear and dispose of the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Suit No. 541 of 2012 and the Arpita Sampatty Prattarpan Suit No. 23 of 2012 analogously in accordance with the provisions of section 17(gha) of the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Ain, 2001.

4. The facts relevant for disposal of the Rule as stated in the Writ Petition are that the land measuring 0.27 acre pertaining to SA Plot No. 2347 under SA Khatian No. 28 corresponding to BS Plot No. 2049 of Mouza-Dottorail, JL No. 62 Police Station, Golapganj, Sylhet (the suit land) has been included in the 'Ka' schedule of vested property list published in serial No. 179 in Bangladesh Gazette Notification dated 19-4-2012. The petitioner as plaintiff on 2-1-2013 filed Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 before the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet for releasing the suit land from the 'K' list of vested property contending, inter alia, that one Moin Charan Shil of Village Dottorail, Golapganj, Sylhet was the original owner of the suit land. Said Moin Charan Shil sold the suit land to Abdul Latif, the predecessor of the petitioner through an unregistered Kabala dated 20-4-1963 on receiving Taka 95 as the consideration of the suit land and delivered possession thereof in his favour. After purchasing the suit land said Abdul Latif constructed a homestead therein. Abdul Latif died leaving behind two sons, namely Mujibur Rahman and Md Ziaur Rahman and three daughters namely Shahida Ali, Wahida Ahmed and Farida Latif as his legal heirs. Subsequently, among the legal heirs of said Abdul Latif the petitioner got exclusive title and possession over the suit land. The petitioner in a formidable circumstances took lease of the suit land in order to maintain his possession. The sole defendant, Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet contested the suit by filing a written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and the suit land has been leased out to the petitioner vide VP Case No. 83 of 1969-70 as the original owner of the suit land left for India leaving the suit land uncared for and the Government became the lawful owner in the suit land and the suit is liable to be dismissed. The Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No.3, Sylhet after hearing the parties dismissed the suit by the judgment and decree dated 19-11-2005. The petitioner having been aggrieved by the said judgment and decree dated 19-11-2015 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No.3, Sylhet moved the appellate forum by filing Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Appeal No. 11 of 2016 wherein the appeal is still pending.

5. The petitioner recently came to know that the respondents No. 5-8 also filed Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Suit No. 541 of 2012 claiming the self-same land for releasing the same from the `Ka' list of vested property wherein the same Tribunal decreed the suit against the defendant, Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet directing to exclude or release the suit land from the 'Ka' list of vested property vide judgment and decree dated 10-3-2016. Having been aggrieved by the said judgment and decree dated 10-3-2016 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet, the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet filed Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Appeal No. 92 of 2016 before the Arpita Sampatty Prattyar-pan Appellate Tribunal, Sylhet who having heard the parties dismissed the appeal on contest by the judgment and decree dated 18-9-2016 and thereby affirmed the judgment and decree dated 10-3-2016 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Prattarpan Additional Tribunal No.3, Sylhet in favour of the respondents No. 5-8. It has further been stated in the Petition that the schedule land of the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 and the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Suit No. 541 of 2012 being same, both the suits should be heard and disposed of analogously by one Tribunal in view of the provisions of section 17(gha) of the Ain, 2001. But the said two suits were heard and disposed of separately by the same Tribunal beyond the knowledge of the petitioner. The petitioner having been aggrieved by the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-9-2016 filed the instant Writ Petition and obtained the Rule and the order of stay as stated above.

6. The respondents Nos. 5-8 entered appearance and contested the Rule by filing an affidavit-in-opposition. The case of the respondents No. 5-8 is that the petitioner has no locus standi to challenge the judgment and decree passed in Arpita Sampatty Prattarn Suit No. 541 of 2012 since he was not party to that proceeding and he did not take any steps at an earliest possible time for analogous hearing of both the suits inasmuch as the provisions of section 17(gha) of the Ain, 2001 is not mandatory one.

7. Mr Sudipta Arjun, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner having placed the provisions of section 17(gha) of the Ain, 2001 submits that the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Tribunal was required by law to hear and dispose of both the Arpita Sampatty Prattarpan Suit No. 541 of 2012 and the Arpita Sampatty Prattarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 analogously since the schedule of both the suits were the same and, as such, the judgment and decree passed in the said two suits are liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and are of no legal effect.

8. The learned Advocate submits further that on setting aside the judgment and decree passed in Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 appeal preferred by the petitioner to the Appellate Tribunal shall stand abated.

9. Mr Surojit Bhattcharjee, learned Advocate appearing for the respondents Nos. 5-8 submits that the petitioner is not competent to file the present Writ Petition challenging the judgment and decree dated 18-9-2016 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Prattyarpan Additional Tribunal No.3, Sylhet since he was not a party to that proceeding.

10. We have considered the submissions of both the parties and perused the provisions of section 17(gha) of the Ain, 2001. The only issue for determination of the Rule is to see whether the impugned judgment and decree dated 18-9-2016 passed by the respondent No.1 is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and whether the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 541 of 2012 and the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 are required to be heard and disposed of analogously in accordance with the provisions of section 17(gha) of the Ain, 2001.

11. Before entering into the factual matter, we need to look into the said provisions of section 17(gha) of the Ain, 2001 which is quoted below for ready reference:

" ১৭। ট্রাইব্যুনাল-

(খ)..............

(গ)..........

(গ)............

(ঘ) উক্ত তালিকায় অন্তর্ভূক্ত কোন সম্পত্তির ব্যাপারে একাধিক ব্যক্তি আবেদন করিলে এইরুপ আবেদন একযোগে শুনানী করিবে এবং প্রয়োজনবোধে একটি রায়ের মাধ্যমে উহাদিগকে নিম্পত্তি করিতে পারিবে”

12. On perusal of the aforesaid provisions of law, it appears that where there are more than one claimants regarding the vested property in that case the concerned Tribunal should hear and dispose of all suits analogously. In the instant case, both the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 541 of 2012 and the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 were filed for releasing the self-same property. One by the petitioner and other by the respondents Nos. 5-8. Wherein the same Tribunal dismissed the suit of the petitioner and decreed the suit of the respondents No. 5-8 thereby two different opinions have been declared by the Tribunal in respect of releasing of the self-same property and in respect of the status of the suit property as to whether the suit property was returnable vested property or not. The provisions of law as quoted above are clearly speaks that with regard to the self-same property if more than one suit is filed those suits are to be heard and disposed of by the Tribunal analogously and if necessary a single judgment may be pronounced on those suits.

About the self-same property there should not be a different opinion with regard to the status of the property.

13. Having considered the provisions of sub-section (gha) of section 17 of the Ain, 2001, we find the provisions is a mandatory one. However, the Court can pass a single or separate judgment with regard to those suits.

<u>14. Since two suits were filed with regard to the self-same property, it was the duty of the Tribunal to hear and dispose of both the suits analogously. It was also the duty of the Tribunal to register both the suits one after another against the serial number of the self-same property mentioned in the Gazette Notification. Considering the provisions of law and the present facts and circumstances of the case, we find a good deal of force in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner and the Rule bears merit.</u>

15. Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute and the application is allowed.

16. The judgment and decree dated 10-3-2016 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet in Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No 541 of 2012 and the judgment and decree dated 18-9-2016 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Appellate Tribunal in Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Appeal No. 92 of 2016 are hereby set-aside. Consequently, the judgment and decree dated 19-11-2015 passed by the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet in Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 is also hereby set-aside.

17. Consequently, the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Appeal No. 11 of 2016 preferred by the petitioner before the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Tribunal, Sylhet stands abated.

18. The Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet is hereby directed to hear and dispose of the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 541 of 2012 and the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Suit No. 23 of 2013 afresh analogously in accordance with the provisions of section 17(gha) of the Ain, 2001.

Communicate the judgment to the Arpita Sampatty Pratttyarpan Additional Tribunal No. 3, Sylhet at once for necessary action.

End.

lawyer:
Shishir Kanti Mazumder, Advocate—For the Petitioner. 

Samarendra Nath Biswas, Assistant Attorney-General—For the Respondents.
parties:
Sarwar Miah (Md) alias Nabab Meah---------Petitioner 
Vs. 
Government of Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary,Ministry of Land, Bangladesh Dhaka and  others-------- Respondents
full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J : This Rule Nisi has been issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order No. 12 dated 28-2-2016 passed by the Judge (Joint District Judge), Land Survey Tribunal, Netrakona in Land Survey Tribunal Case No. 580 of 2014 for depositing remaining Court fee amounting to Taka 700 as per Article 12(ii) of the Second Schedule of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as amended on in August 2010 fixing Court fees of Taka 1,000 (Annexure-B) should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority is of no legal effect, and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. The facts relevant for the disposal of the Rule, in short, is that the land of Baratali Mouja under Mohongonj Upazila of Netrakona District being SA Khatian No. 577 in SA Plot No. 292/293 and BRS Khatian No.250 in BRS Plot No. 502/503 measuring 0.40 acres of land were recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendant Nos. 1-6 and their predecessors while have been in possession thereof sold the same in favour of the plaintiff and his brother on 3-10-1970 and accordingly the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing 0.20 acres of land and that during BRS, record of right the aforesaid land has been wrongly recorded in the name of the predecessor of the defendants which are mistakenly held and correction of the same is necessary and hence the petitioner has filed Land Survey Tribunal Case No. 580 of 2014 under section 145A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. At the time of filing the Land Survey Tribunal Case on 29-1-2014, the petitioner furnished Court fee of Taka 300 and the same was accepted accordingly. The defendants appeared before the tribunal and they by filing a compromise petition on 30-3-2014 accepted the claim of the plaintiff and pursuant to a Solehnama both the parties adduced evidence on 15-9-2014. On 28-2-2016 the learned tribunal accepted the Solehnama, but passed an order to the effect that as per Article 12(ii) of the Schedule-II of the Court-Fees Act, 1870 as amended on 1-8-2008 and coming in to force on 1-9-2010 Court fee would be Taka 1,000, but the case has been filed with the Court fee of Taka 300 only and there remains outstanding Court fee of Taka 700 and directed the plaintiff to pay a remaining Court fee of Taka 700 within 21 (twenty one) working days, failing which the plaint shall stand rejected. The petitioner challenging this order has filed this writ petition and obtained Rule and order of stay.

3. Mr Shishir Kanti Mazumder, the learned advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submits that Article 12(ii) of the Schedule-II of the Court-Fees (Amendment) Act, 2010 would not be applicable in respect the Land Survey Tribunal Cases as the Tribunal Cases are not the suits as enumerated in the said provision of Article 12(ii) and hence fixing Court fees of Taka 1,000 and direction to deposit remaining Court fees of Taka 700 are illegal and without lawful authority. He further submits that by filing tribunal case the petitioner did not seek alter or cancel any entry in the register as alleged in Article 12(ii) of the Schedule-II of the Court-Fees (Amendment) Act, 2010 and hence the aforesaid provision does not lie in respect of filing Land Survey Tribunal Cases and thus the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been issued without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. He further submits that in many districts the Land Survey Tribunal are accepting the cases furnishing Tala 300 of Court fees, so the impugned order is liable to be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect.

4. Mr Samarendra Nath Biswas, the learned Assistant Attorney-General though did not file any Vokalatnama on behalf of the respondents, but with the leave of the Court he submits that as per Court-Fees (Amendment) Act, 2010 the petitioner is liable to pay Court fees of Taka 1,000, because this is a case of alteration or cancellation of any entry in the register and thus as per law the petitioner is liable to pay the aforesaid Court fee and as such the Rule is liable to be discharged.

5. We have gone through the writ petition and the annexures annexed thereto as well as the relevant laws. We have also considered the submissions of the learned advocates for both the parties. The only question is to be decided whether the impugned order was justified or passed in accordance with law. Let us examine the law first. Article 12(ii) of the Schedule II of the Court-Fees (Amendment) Act, 2010 runs as follows:

"to alter or cancel any entry in a register of the names of proprietors of revenue paying estates, should have to be paid at the rate of Taka 1,000."

6. It is very clear that if anything has been recorded in the register and the plaintiff files any application or suit or case to alter or cancel the register, the Court fee should have to be paid of Taka 1,000 as per provision of Article 12(ii) of schedule II of the Court-Fees Act, 2010 (Amended). Now, the question is what is the meaning of "proprietor", "revenue paying estates" and the "register"? The legal definition of register is agenda, album, almanac, archive, arrangement, balance sheet, calendar, catalogue, chronicle, chronology, day book, diary, docket, ephemeris, file, journal, ledger, liber, list, loc, log book, minutes, notes, proceedings, record, registration book, roll, roster, schedule, tabulate, written record. The definition of proprietor has been defined in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950.

7. The meaning of 'proprietor' is given in definition clause-2(20) of the said Act which runs as follows:

"Proprietor" means a person owning, whether in trust or for his own benefit, an estate or a part of an estate."

8. Now let us see what is the meaning of the estate? The meaning of 'estate' is given in definition clause 2(11) of the said Act which runs as follows:

"Estate" means land included under one entry in any of the general Registers of revenue-paying lands and revenue-free lands, prepared and maintained under the law for the time being in force by the Collector of a districts, and includes Government khas mahals and revenue-free lands not entered in any register."

9. Now let us see, what is the case for? From the annexure-A, it appears that it was the case for “রেকর্ড সংশোধনের মোকদ্দমা. In the plaint in paragraph-3 it has been mentioned that “অত্রাদালতের এলাকাধীন বিগত ১৫-১১-২০১৩ তারিখে রেকর্ড সংশোধনের সরকারি প্রজ্ৰাপন প্রচারিত হওয়ায় জানিতে পারায় অত্র মোকদ্দমার কারণ উত্তব হইয়াছে। দাবীর ভূমির বর্তমান বাজার মূল্য ২০,০০০ টাকা রেকর্ড সংশোধনের মোকদ্দমা বিধায় নির্দিষ্ট কোর্ট ফি যোগে অত্র মোকদমা দায়ের করা হইল। In the prayer portion of the plaint, the plaintiff mentioned that খরিদা ২০ শতাংশ ভূমিতে পৃথক রেকর্ড হওয়ার মর্মে সংশোধনের আদেশ সূচক ডিক্রি দিতে.”

<u>10. From the above mentioned prayers and statements made in the plaint it is very clear that it was the case for correction of the record. What is record? We have already stated that the register means record. From the definition of register it is found that record means register. Since record is the register, as per said Article 12(ii) it is also clear that, to alter or cancel any entry in the register of the names of proprietors of revenue paying estates Court fees must be paid as per provision of Article 12(ii) of the Schedule 2 of the Court-Fees Act as amended in 2010. Since the petitioner is the proprietor of a particular estate and he has prayed for correction of the record which is a register. The learned judge of the Land Survey Tribunal, Netrakona has passed a very correct order to pay Court fee of Taka 1,000, which is legal and has been passed in accordance with law. There is nothing to interfere with this order.</u>

11. Mr Shishir Kanti Mazumder, the learned advocate has apprised this Court that in many districts the learned Judges of the Land Survey Tribunals are receiving Taka 300 fixed Court fee in land survey tribunal cases. It is very unfortunate, why the judges cannot understand the clear mandate of law. Thus, we are of the view that the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, Law and Justice

Division should inform the Judges of the Land Survey Tribunals all over the country to accept the plaint with the Court fee's of Taka 1000 in the cases for correction of record referring this judgment.

12. With the above observations and direction the Rule is discharged, however, without any order as to cost.

13. The office is directed to communicate a copy of this judgment to the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Law and Justice Division as soon as possible.

The Land Survey Tribunal, Netrakona is directed to receive the remaining Court fees of Taka 700 within 2 (two) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this judgment.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 391-92 of 2010.
lawyer:
Sirajul Haque, Senior Advocate instructed by Md Nurul Islam Chowdhury, Advocate-on-Record ---------For the Petitioner (in both the cases). 
None Represented -------- For Respondents (in both the cases).
parties:
AKM Jalaluddin Ahmed -------- Petitioner (in both the cases)
VS
Bangladesh, represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Education and others ---------- Respondents (in both the cases)
full_judgment:
Md Abdul Wahhab Miah J : These two civil petitions for leave to appeal have arisen out of the same decision dated the 24th day of November, 2004 passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in Administrative Appellate Tribunal Appeal Nos.208 of 2004 and 197 of 2004 allowing the same and are disposed of by this common judgment.

2. Facts necessary for disposal of these petitions are that the petitioner filed an application before the Administrative Tribunal under section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act, 1980) (at the relevant time, there was only one Tribunal) impleading the respondents herein as opposite parties for declaration that the order as contained in Memo No.Sec-2/ Misc-19/2000/4931Edu dated 18-7-2001 passed by opposite party No. 1, respondent No. I herein (hereinafter referred to as opposite party No. 1), rejecting the appeal and the order contained in Memo No. DIA/99/1-C- 18/Admn-Part 11/417/6 dated 30-3-2000 passed by opposite party No.2, respondent No.2 herein (hereinafter referred to as opposite party No.2), dismissing the petitioner from service as illegal, void, not binding upon him, and he is still in service and also for a direction upon the opposite parties to reinstate him in service and give him all attending benefits admissible under the Rules. The application was registered as Administrative Tribunal Case No.2002 of 2001. Eventually the case was transferred to Administrative Tribunal No.2, Dhaka and was renumbered as Administrative Tribunal Case No. 192 of 2003.

3. The case of the petitioner was that he joined the service on 1-9-1971 as Lower Division Assistant under the Education Directorate, erstwhile East Pakistan. The petitioner since then had been serving honestly and diligently to the satisfaction of the higher authority, and due to his good performance in the service, he was promoted to the post of Upper Division Assistant on 4-5-1987 and to the post of Auditor on 18-2-1985. The petitioner while serving as Auditor in the Directorate of Inspection and Audit, there was serious dissatisfaction amongst the officers and the employees against Mr Atahar Ali Dewan, Director of Inspection and Audit, and subsequently, the petitioner along with other five employees was placed under suspension by the said Director of Inspector and Audit. While the petitioner was serving in the Directorate of Inspector and Audit, he received a charge sheet containing 19 charges on the allegations of misconduct, negligence of duty, inefficiency, unruliness etc. The petitioner was asked to show cause as to why he shall-not be dismissed from service. The petitioner filed an application on 1-9-1999 requesting the authority to supply him certain papers for taking proper defence, but copies of the papers sought were not supplied to him. Thereafter, the petitioner submitted his written defence denying the allegations made in the charge sheet, but the authority without considering the written defence of the petitioner constituted a Board of Inquiry on 1-9-1999 consisting of 3(three) members headed by Dr Md Abdul Motaleb; Deputy Director (Dhaka Division) as its Chairman. The petitioner and others filed an application to the Chairman of the Board of Inquiry with specific allegation of no confidence against the Chairman and one of the members of that Board, but no action was taken in that regard. However, the petitioner being directed by the Board of Inquiry, appeared before the Inquiry Officer along with defence witnesses. The Board of Inquiry recorded the statements of the petitioner and his witnesses in between 7-11-1999 to 18-11-1999 in the absence of the complainant, or any conducting officer on behalf of the prosecution. The petitioner was not also given any opportunity by the Inquiry Officer to consult the relevant papers. The Board of Inquiry also recorded the statements of the prosecution witnesses behind the back of the petitioner and he was not allowed to cross examine the witnesses adduced against him. The Board of Inquiry most illegally took statements beyond the knowledge of the petitioner, and accordingly, they submitted a perverse and frivolous report finding him guilty of the charge brought against him. Opposite party No.2 on the basis, of the illegal inquiry report issued the 2nd show cause notice upon the petitioner proposing major penalty of dismissal from service under rule 4(2)(d) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 1985 and accordingly, on receipt of the 2nd show cause notice, the petitioner submitted his written reply to the authority on 16-2-2000 pleading his innocence, but opposite party No.2 most illegally and without lawful authority passed the impugned order on 30-3-2000 dismissing the petitioner from service.

4. Against the order of dismissal, the petitioner, preferred an appeal to the appellate authority which was rejected by opposite party No. 1 by his office order dated 18-7-2001 and hence, the application.

5. Opposite party No.1 (before the Administrative Tribunal) contested the case by filing a written statement denying the material allegations made in the application and contending, inter alia, that the case was not maintainable in its present form, there was no cause of action to file the case, the case was bad for defect of party and it was also barred by limitation. A serious dissatisfaction arose amongst the employees, and the then Director Atahar Ali Dewan on different matters and the employees informed the matter to the Ministry of Education, but at one stage five employees including the petitioner were placed under suspension by the said Director on the allegation of misconduct. Charge was framed against the petitioner asking him to show cause is as to why he would not be dismissed from service. Accordingly, the petitioner showed his-cause in writing, but was not being satisfactory, the concerned-authority constituted a Board of Inquiry consisting there-members headed by Dr. Md Abdul Motaleb Deputy Director as Chairman of that committee. The Board of inquiry held inquiry from 8-9-1999 to 30-1-2000 giving opportunity to the petitioner of self-defence and submitted its report finding him guilty of the charges brought against him. Thereafter, the authority issued the 2nd show cause notice upon the petitioner proposing major penalty. The petitioner submitted his written reply to the show cause notice. The authority passed the impugned order dismissing the petitioner from service by observing all requirements of law. Against the order of dismissal, the petitioner filed departmental appeal to the Secretary, Ministry of Education and it was rejected after due consideration. There was no irregularity and illegality in the departmental proceeding and, as such, the impugned order passed by the authority was quite legal which did not call for any interference by the tribunal. The case of the petitioner was totally misconceived and thus it was liable to be dismissed.

6. The Administrative Tribunal by its order dated 4-8-2004 allowed the application in part, set aside the order dated 30-3-2000 passed by opposite party No.2 dismissing him from service and the order dated 18-7-2001 issued by opposite party No.1 rejecting the appeal. The Tribunal further, directed the opposite parties to reinstate the petitioner in service from the date of his dismissal treating the period of absence of the petitioner from service as extraordinary leave without pay (without break in service). Against the order of the Administrative Tribunal, the opposite parties (before the Administrative Tribunal) filed Administrative Tribunal Appeal No. 197 of 2004 before the Administrative Appellate; Tribunal, Dhaka (hereinafter referred to as the Appellate Tribunal). The petitioner also filed Administrative Appellate Tribunal Appeal No.208 of 2004 before the Appellate Tribunal. The Appellate Tribunal by the impugned decision allowed Appeal No. 197 of 2004 and dismissed Appeal No.208 of 2004; hence these two leave petitions.

7. Heard Mr Sirajul Hoque, learned Counsel, appearing for the petitioner in both the petitions, perused the impugned decision passed, by the Appellate Tribunal.

8. From the decision of the Appellate Tribunal, it appears that it dismissed the appeal on the ground that the same was filed after 9 (nine) months and 5 (five) days of 'the period of limitation. In calculating the period of limitation, the Appellate Tribunal found that the authority dismissed the petitioner from service on 3-3-2000, he preferred the departmental appeal against the order of dismissal before the appellate authority on 7-5-2000, the appeal was deemed to have been rejected on 7-7-2002 by operation of law, although the authority formally rejected the appeal on 18-7-2001.

<u>9. Mr Sirajul Hoque relying on the 3rd proviso to sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Act, 1980 has submitted that since in the instant case, the appeal filed by the petitioner was formally rejected on 18-7-2001 that should be date of the cause of action to file the application before the Administrative Tribunal, but the Appellate Tribunal wrongly counted the date of limitation from the date of expiry of two months from the date of filing the departmental appeal before the appellate authority as provided in the 2nd proviso to sub-section (2) and thus acted illegally in dismissing the appeal on the ground of limitation and, as such, the impugned decision is not sustainable in law.</u>

<u>10. This Court in a number of cases earlier decided that it is the 2nd proviso to sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Act, 1980 read with the period of limitation as mentioned in the 3rd proviso, i.e. two months plus six months which shall govern the period of limitation in filing an application before the Administrative Tribunal and a case filed before the Administrative Tribunal after the expiry of the said period (two months + six months) shall be barred by limitation.</u>

11. We do not see any reason to review the said decision of this Court. Therefore, we find nothing wrong with the view taken by the Appellate Tribunal that the case filed before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation.

12. Mr Sirajul Haque also tried to argue another point that limitation is a mixed question of fact and law. The opposite parties (before the Administrative Tribunal) did not raise any objection before the Administrative Tribunal about the limitation in filing the case before it, therefore, at the appellate stage, they were not entitled to take the said point. It is true that the limitation is a mixed question of fact and law, and that should be taken in the Court of first instance, but there may be cases in which no fact need be gone into and if it is found from the facts stated by the petitioner that a case is filed beyond the period of limitation, particularly in a case under the special statute like the instant one, then we do not find any legal bar to raise the point of limitation even at the appellate stage. When admittedly, the case in hand was filed before the Administrative Tribunal long after the period of six months after the expiry of the period of two months from the date of filing the departmental appeal as provided in the second proviso to sub-section (2) of section 4 of the Act, the opposite parties appellant could very much raise the point of limitation in the appeal and the Appellate Tribunal rightly entertained the same, and decided the point against the petitioner.

In view of the above, we find no merit in the leave petitions and accordingly, both the petitions are dismissed.

End.
