full_judgment:
AKM Abdul Hakim J: This Rule is directed against the order No. 20 dated 21-3-2019 passed by the learned Joint District Judge First Court Dhaka in Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 rejecting an application filed by the defendant-petitioner under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint of the plaintiffs-opposite parties for lack of jurisdiction.

2. The opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 on 22-6-2017 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka impleading the petitioner as sole defendant. The Plaintiff No. 1 claiming a sum of Taka 107,730,854.01 and Plaintiff No. 2 claimed a sum of US $ 3,045,070.77 equivalent to BDT 245,889,465 in total Taka 353,620,319.01 only.

3. The Plaint case in short, are that the First Plaintiff, Tiger IT Bangladesh Limited ("Tiger IT") is a company incorporated under the laws of Bangladesh with its address as set out in the cause title and which carries on the business of information technology and software development; that the Second Plaintiff, Decatur Europe Limited ("Decatur") is a company incorporated under the laws of England with its address as set out in the cause title and carries on business of supplying ancillary equipment and materials used for information technology and for hardware and software development; that the Defendant, Oberthur Technologies Societe Anonyme ("Oberthur") is a company incorporated under the laws of France registered with the Registry of Commerce and Companies of Nanterre under the identification number 340-709-534 with its address as set out in the cause title carrying on business in the field of digital security and identification technologies in Bangladesh and elsewhere; that in anticipation of participation in a Tender for the Bangladesh Election Commission ("BEC") for production of Smart National ID Cards, one Ziaur Rahman, Chairman of the First and Second Plaintiffs, Tiger IT and Decatur, by a letter dated 23-6-2014 ("Discount Letter") offered a discount to the Defendant Oberthur in the sum of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million) only in consideration of the successful participation in the performance of the tender if the tender was awarded to the Defendant; that the terms of the Discount Letter was accepted by Oberthur and formed a contract between each of Tiger IT and Decatur on the one hand and Oberthur on the other; that Tiger IT and Decatur entered into a contract with Oberthur dated 29-7-2014 for Solution Development, Hardware and Services Purchase Agreement being Contract No. OT-2014-638 ("Tiger IT Contract"); that on 29-7-2014, Decatur entered into a Purchase Agreement with Oberthur being Contract No. OT-2014-928 ("Decatur Contract"); that the prices set out in the Tiger IT Contract and the Decatur Contract incorpo-rated the discount of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million) only split roughly as to US $ 1.5 million to Tiger IT and US $ 3.5 million to Decatur. As a result, Oberthur got benefit of the discount of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million Only) pursuant to the Discount Letter; that the bid was submitted by Oberthur was accepted by the BEC and an award was made by the BEC to Oberthur in December 2014; that the Tiger IT Contract and Decatur Contract were amended by further agreements dated 16-3-2015; that Oberthur failed to comply with the obligations set out in Tiger IT Contract and in the Decatur Contract leading to their termination Tiger IT and by Decatur by two letters dated 10-8-2016 and 4-8-2016 respectively. Accordingly, the terms of the Discount Letter were not complied with since Oberthur failed to purchase all the materials that were included in the BOM; that in the circumstances, Oberthur was not entitled to the discount of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million) only as agreed in the Discount Letter; that the First Plaintiff, Tiger IT has calculated that out of the said total discount of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million) only the sum of BDT 107,730,854.01 (Bangladesh Taka One Hundred Seven Million, Seven Hundred Thirty Thousand, Eight Hundred Fifty Four and one Paisa) is the discount that the Defendant is not entitled to as a result of its breach of the Discount Letter.

4. The Second Plaintiff, Decatur has calculated that out of the said total discount of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million) only the sum of US $ 3,045,070.77 (United States Dollars Three Million Forty Five Thousand Seventy and Seventy Seven cents) equivalent to BDT 245,889,465 (Taka Two Hundred Forty Five Million Eight Hundred Eighty Nine Thousand Four Hundred Sixty Five © US $ 1 = BDT80.75) is the discount that the Defendant is not entitled to as a result of its breach of the Discount Letter. The Plaintiffs claim the said sums stated in paragraph Nos. 13 and 14 of the plaint together with interest pendent lite and until payment at the rate of 10% percent per annum or as per the law of the country.

5. That the cause of action in the suit arose on 23-62014 when Mr Ziaur Rahman, Chairman of the First and Second Plaintiffs, offered a Discount Letter to the Defendant Oberthur in the sum of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million) only, on 29-7-2014 when the First and Second Plaintiff entered into a contract with the Defendant for Solution Development, Hardware and Services Purchase Agreement, on 29-7-2014 when Second Plaintiff entered into a Purchase Agreement with the Defendant, on December 2014 when BEC passed an award in favour of Defendant, on 16-3-2015 when The Tiger IT Contract and Decatur Contract were amended by further agreements on 10-8-2016 and 4-8-2016 respectively when the Plaintiffs terminated Tiger IT Contract and Decatur Contract due to the Defendant's failure to comply with the obligations set out in Tiger IT Contract and in the Decatur Contract by two letters being dated 10-8-2016 and 4-8-2016 and the cause of action is still continuing till date of filing the Plaint. With these averments the plaintiffs filed the present suit.

6. During pendency of the suit, Defendant on 17-7-2018 filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint, stating, inter alia, that the plaintiff-petitioner filed the Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka Bangladesh for its realization of money amounting to BDT 107,730,845.01 and US $ 3,045,070.77 equivalent to Taka 245,889,465 in total equivalent to BDT 353,620,319.01 only that on 29th day of July 2014 Oberthur Technologies SA a French Societe Anonyme having its registered office at 420, rued' Estienne d'Orves 92700 Colombes, France duly entered into agreements with each of the Plaintiffs, each name "SOLUTION DEVELOPMENT, HARDWARE AND SERVICE PURCHASE AGREEMENT". The agreements were for the supply of goods and services relating to a Tender for the Bangladesh Election Commission ("BEC") for the production of Smart National ID Cards. The agreements were varied by subsequent deeds of variation entered into between the parties on 16-3-2015. The plaintiffs issued two letters to the defendant unilaterally termination the contracts on 10-8-2016 and 4-8-2016 that after issuance of the termination letter the plaintiff filed the instant suit before the Joint District Judge, First Court, Dhaka having suit valuation at EDT 353,620,319.01.

7. That the defendant hereby file this application challenging the jurisdiction of the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka Bangladesh as the dispute arose out of an agreement entered between the parties where the Agreements contains an Article stated below on the application law and jurisdiction (Appendix 3, 3A, 4, 4A of the plaintiff's application).

Agreement with plaintiff No. 1 dated 29th July 2014 states as below:  "ARTICLE 19 APPLICABLE LAW 19.1 Any dispute arising between the parties over the construction, validity, performance or non performance, or ceasing of this agreement shall be subject to the sole competence of the competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland 19.2 This Agreement will be governed, construed and enforced with the laws of Switzerland (without giving effect to its conflict of law principles) the parties agree that the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sales of Goods shall not apply to this Agreement."

Agreement with plaintiff No. 2 dated 29th July 2014 states as below:  "ARTICLE 9 APPLICABLE LAW 9.1 Any dispute arising between the parties over the construction, validity, performance or non performance, or ceasing of this agreement shall be subject to the sole competence of the competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland 9.2 This Agreement will be governed; construed and enforced with the laws of Switzerland (without giving effect to its conflict of law principle) The parties agree that the 1980 United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sales of Goods shall not apply to this Agreement." Added of variation to the Agreement with plaintiff No. 1 dated: 29th July 2014,  dated 16th March 2015 states as below:

3. GOVERNING LAW

This deed and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation (including non-contractual disputes or claims) shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of Switzerland.

Deed of variation to the Agreement with plaintiff No. 2 dated :  29th July 2014, dated 16th July 2015  states as below:  "4. GOVERNING LAW This deed and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it or its subject matter or formation (including non-contractual dispute or claims) shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the law of Switzerland.

5. JURISDICTION.

Each party irrevocable agrees that the competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this deed or its subject matter or formation (including non-contractual disputes or claims)"

8. By filing this application, the defendant in no way submits to the jurisdiction of the First Joint District judge of Dhaka, Bangladesh. That the claim upon which this instant suit is brought before the Hon'ble Court does not fall under jurisdiction of the said Court because:

a. The claim relates to the agreements of 29-7-2014 which each contain clauses stating that any dispute "shall be subject to the sole competence of the competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland";

b. The claim does not relate to the deeds of variation of 16-3-2015 that varied certain terms of the agreements of 29-7-2014 has been brought in breach of the aforementioned provisions of the relevant contracts; and c. The claim has therefore been brought in breach of the provisions of the agreements of 29-7-2014, and thus the suit is not maintainable in the manner and capacity it has proceeded in so far.

9. Plaintiffs contested the said application by filing written objection dated 2-1-2019 denying the material allegations made in the application and contending, inter-alia that, the statements made in paragraph No. 3 of the Order VII, rule 11 of the application, in so far as they state that the "defendant" decided to challenge the jurisdiction of the court, are incorrect assertions and, as such, are denied. The plaintiffs firmly states that the defendant has submitted to the jurisdiction of the court in the instant suit and has waived the contractual right to object to jurisdiction. The plaintiffs further state that the defendant's objection as to the jurisdiction of the court in respect of the instant suit will not be maintainable under section 21 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 ("CPC") as such objection was not made at the earliest opportunity by the defendant. The plaintiffs lastly state that the defendant's application has been made improperly and hence is liable to be rejected; that the statements made in paragraph No. 4 of the Application, insofar as they restate certain provisions of the Tiger Contract and Decatur contract as amended by the Deeds of Variation dated 16-3-2015 as being grounds for the defendant objecting to the jurisdiction of the learned Court, are baseless and are as such denied; that the provisions of the Tiger Contract and Decatur Contract and the Deeds of Variation dated 16-3-2015 subsequently varying these contracts that have been quoted by the defendant in the said paragraph go to show that the courts of Geneva, Switzerland have a non-exclusive jurisdiction in the instant case, thus rendering discretion to the plaintiffs to file the instant suit before the court the defendant has already submitted to the jurisdiction of the court by conduct and by failing to submit an objection to the jurisdiction as to the place of suing at the earliest possible opportunity under section 21 of CPC. As such, the defendant is barred by section 21 of the CPC as well as by the doctrine of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel from bringing any objection as to the place of suing at this stage of the suit; that the plaintiffs filed the instant suit before the court on 22-6-2017; that the service of summons of the suit was duly effected by the process server of the court on 15-8-2017 and the court recorded confirmation of service of summons upon the defendant by its order No. 7 dated 11-1-2018; that the defendant filed appearance in the suit for the first time on 5-2-2018, and then subsequently on 2-4-2018, praying for more time on both instances; that the defendant did not even appear on the due date on 20-6-2018; that the defendant filed an application under Order VII, rule 11 on 17-7-2018 i.e. more than 9 months after receiving summonses of the suit and more than 5 months after first filing appearance in the suit; that in the meantime, the defendant on 6-6-2018 filed a suit having claim No. CL-2018-000390 in the Commercial Court Queen's Bench Division, High Court of Justice in London, United Kingdom (hereinafter "the English Proceedings") against the plaintiffs and one Mr Ziaur Rahman, who is the Chairman of both the plaintiff-companies, praying for an injunction against them from commencing or supporting the continuation of legal proceedings in Bangladesh for allegedly being in breach of exclusive jurisdiction provisions in relevant agreements and further praying for a direction upon the instant plaintiffs to discontinue the proceedings of the instant suit in Dhaka, Bangladesh; that in the said suit in the English proceedings, the instant defendant contended that the parties were under an obligation under Clauses 19.1 of both the Tiger Contract and Decatur Contract (as varied by the Deeds of Variation dated 16-3-2015) to only bring proceedings arising out of the said contracts within "the exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Geneva, Switzerland". The instant defendant further alleged in the English Proceedings that the filing of the instant suit constituted a breach of that contractual obligation by the instant plaintiffs; that the instant defendant also sought in the English Proceedings for an interim injunction upon the instant plaintiffs and Mr Ziaur Rahman, essentially to bar them from proceeding with the instant suit and other proceedings in Bangladesh Courts in alleged breach of the exclusive jurisdiction provision in the aforesaid contracts; that the instant defendant's application for interim injunction under the English Proceedings was refused by Mr Justice Knowles of the Commercial Court, Queen's Bench Division, High Court of Justice in London, United Kingdom on 15-6-2018.

10. That it is clear that instead of raising an objection as to the place of suing before the court in the instant suit at the earliest possible opportunity as per section 21 of CPC, the instant defendant rather sought, and is presently actively seeking to stop, injunct, restrain, and debar the instant plaintiffs from continuing with the instant suit before the court though inviting intervention from a court of a foreign jurisdiction over the suit proceedings in the instant court.

11. That it should further be stated that the plaintiffs' claims in the instant suit relate in the first place to the Discount Letter dated 23-62014, which contains no provisions regarding applicable law and jurisdiction. The Discount Letter that was concluded on 23-6-2014 between the plaintiffs and the defendant in Dhaka, Bangladesh, relates to the project carried out in Bangladesh (Production and Distribution of Smart NID Cards for Citizens of Bangladesh) and was performed in Bangladesh. Secondly, the plaintiffs' claims upon which the instant suit is brought relate to subject matter of the Deeds of Variation dated 16-3-2015, which varied the Tiger Contract and the Decatur Contract. The defendant has itself admitted in paragraph No. 2 of their Order VII, rule 11 application that the "agreements" being the Tiger Contract and the Decatur Contract, "were varied by subsequent deeds of variation entered into between the parties on 16-3-2015". Clauses 6.1 and 5.1 respectively of the said Deeds of Variation dated 16-3-2015 states that "the competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this deed or its subject matter or formation including non-contractual disputes or claims". Hence, there is no scope for the defendant to suggest that the plaintiffs were under a contractual obligation under the aforesaid contracts to bring the claim in the instant suit only before competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland. Rather, since the jurisdiction of the courts in Geneva, Switzerland is non-exclusive, the plaintiff was not contractually barred from bringing the instant suit before the court; that there can be no dispute that the trial court has the right and proper pecuniary, territorial and subject-matter jurisdiction to hear the instant suit under the Civil Courts Act, 1887. The defendant's only objection as to the jurisdiction of the trial court in respect of the instant suit arises out of an alleged contractual obligation between plaintiffs and the defendant to bring the claim under this suit in the courts of Geneva, Switzerland. The plaintiffs contend that the contractual obligations of the plaintiffs do not bar the plaintiffs from bringing the instant suit before the trial court. However, even if it were to be considered that the plaintiffs were barred under their respective contractual obligations from bringing that instant suit before the trail Court. The defendant subsequently waived-off the benefits of such contractual obligation and acquiescenced to the jurisdiction of this Court by failing to raise any objection as to the jurisdiction of the Court for 9 months after being informed about the suit and for 5 months after first filing appearance in the suit despite taking steps in the instant suit. Thus, the defendant's objection as to the jurisdiction of this Court in respect of the instant suit is barred by application of the doctrine of waiver, acquiescence and estoppel.

12. That the defendant ought to have raised objection as to the jurisdiction of this court as soon as it become aware of the instead proceedings. Instead, the defendant had refrained from filing any objection as to jurisdiction when its learned lawyers filed appearance on 5-2-2018, 2-4-2018, 20-6-2018 and on other "off-dates" without offering any explanation for why they failed to file such objection earlier.

13. That it should also be mentioned that the defendant has not challenged the jurisdiction of the learned court in the proper form and manner by improperly filing the instant application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure seeking for rejection of the plaint of the instant suit on the alleged, but baseless grounds that this court does not have the jurisdiction. The instant suit cannot be rejected under Order VII, rule 11 as it does not satisfy any of the criteria laid out in its sub-sections; that it is stated that a suit cannot be "rejected" under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 on the alleged grounds of a court lacking jurisdiction to try the suit; that it is stated that as per judgments in 49 DLR (AD) 187 and 22 DLR (SC) 334, it is a well-established principle that parties cannot by agreement divest or oust a court of jurisdiction when it possesses jurisdiction under ordinary law, and, as such, the defendant's application is liable to be rejected; that it is humbly submitted that the defendant is not barred by its contractual obligations under the Tiger Contract and the Decatur contract as amended by the Deeds of Variation dated 16-3-2015) from bringing the instant suit before this court and the contentions of the defendant in the application are baseless and legally untenable and hence the said the application is liable to be rejected.

14. That after hearing the parties, the learned Joint District Judge by the impugned order dated 21-3-2019 pleased to reject the application on the findings that the main ground embodied in the Contract between the parties dated 29-7-2014, it appears that if any dispute arisen between them, would be decided by competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland. On perusal of record, it transpires that although in main contract, competent Courts Geneva, Switzerland would be the forum for adjudication of a dispute arising out of the contract but later a Deed of Variation (DoV) dated 16-3-2015 was executed between that parties wherein it was stipulated "The Competent Courts of Geneva, Switzerland shall have non-exclusive Jurisdiction" to settle any dispute on claim arising out of or in connection with this deed or it subject matter or formation (including non-contractual dispute and claims), therefore, the jurisdiction is exclusive or non-exclusive, there is no scope to decide this matter before taking evidence. Moreover, the defendant, who challenged the jurisdiction of this Court, but they filed suit in the Commercial Court, Queen's Bench Division; High Court of Justice in London against claim No. CH 2018000390, same also cannot be decided without taking evidence. With the above findings, learned Joint District Judge rejected the defendant's application that none of the ingredients of Order VII, rule 11 is available, as such same is rejected.

15. Being aggrieved by the Judgment and order dated 21-3-2019, defendant-petitioner, who thereupon moved this court under section 115(1) of the Civil Procedure Code and obtained the present rule and stay.

16. Learned Advocate for the defendant-petitioners, Mr Md Asaduzzaman firstly submits that in the contract it was embodied that any, dispute/claim arising between the parties of the Contract and involving any breach of its terms would be decided by the Competent Courts of Geneva, Switzerland and that such a claim would be governed by the Swiss law. It was contented that in the aforesaid premises, no suit could be instituted against the defendant in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka in Bangladesh, in violation of the above mentioned terms of the Contract. Secondly, it was further submitted that defendant-petitioner Idemia France SAS (formerly Oberthur Technologies Societe Anonyme) with whom the Contract was entered into by the plaintiffs was a company incorporated under the law of France, having registered office in France and was therefore, a non-resident foreign company. Thus a Court in Bangladesh, had no jurisdiction to try the suit against the defendant which was a foreign company. In support of this submission, learned Advocate cited the following decisions reported in 1966 AIR 155, 17 BLD (AD) 249 = 49 DLR (AD) 187, AIR 1980 SC 1239, AIR 1950.

17. Mr Tanjib-ul-Alam, appearing on behalf of the plaintiffs-opposite parties has urged that the plaintiffs filed the present Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka claiming that as per agreement dated 23-6-2016 (Discount Letter) and not under the agreement dated 29-7-2014 and admittedly both the Contract were have subsequently been varied by signing of the Deed of Variation dated 16-3-2015. He further argued that exclusive Jurisdiction claim in the agreements were amended by signing Deed of Variation dated 16-3-2015, so the clause of exclusive jurisdiction become non-exclusive by the amended agreement, which cannot be decided in the proceeding under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure but after taking evidence in the trial of suit. He finally submits that the jurisdiction of local Courts was not ousted. Learned Advocate to substantiate his submissions has referred few decisions and those are as follows: 1) 22 DLR (SC) 334, 2) 1997 BLD (AD) 249, 3) 63 DLR (AD) 138, 4) 18 DLR 709, 5) 53 DLR (AD) 12.

18. It appears that the instant suit was filed on 22-6-2017 and defendant appeared in the suit on 5-2-2018. The defendant filed the application under Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejecting the plaint on 17-7-2018, more than after 9 months after receiving summons of the suit and more than 5 months after appearance in the suit. In the application it was contended, inter-alia, that the claim upon which the present suit is filed before the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka have no jurisdiction/lack of jurisdiction and the claim relates to the agreements dated 29-7-2014 that any dispute shall be subject to the sole competence of the competent Courts of Geneva, Switzerland, that the claim does not relate to the deeds of Variation of 16-3-2015 that varied certain terms of the agreements of 29-7-2014 has been brought in breach of the provisions of the relevant contracts and thus the suit is not maintainable. Accordingly, prayed that the First Court of Joint District Judge Dhaka Bangladesh lacks jurisdiction and, as such, the plaint is liable to be rejected.

19. It further appears that the petitioner filed Supplementary-Affidavit dated 5-2-2020 stating that during pendency of Money Suit No. 62 of 2017, opposite party No. 1, Tiger IT filed another Money Suit No. 62 of 2019 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka stating that the present petitioner entered into purchase agreement dated 29-7-2014 for purchase of Hologram for onward supply to the Election Commission. The said purchase agreement was subsequently amended by a Deed of Variation (DoV) dated 16-3-2015. By executing the said agreement the petitioner agreed to purchase 90 million holograms from the Decatur and it by an agreement dated 11-6-2019, Decatur sold, assigned and transferred to the present opposite party No. 1 plaintiff No. 1, Tiger IT, the right to recover its claim from the instant petitioner in consideration of fixed price US $ 100,000 alongwith 10% service fee and by dint of said assigned agreement parties have also chosen forum clause choosing the Swiss Court Jurisdiction under the Swiss law is not opposed to any public policy or in contravention of the provisions of section 28 of the Contract Act, 1872.

20. Now, the plaintiffs denied that there is no nexus with the agreements dated 29-7-2014 and Deed of Variation (DoV) dated 16-3-2015 and claimed that the present suit being Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 filed in Bangladesh only for payment of the discount amount of US $ 5,000,000 (United States Dollars Five Million) only by the defendant, which is apparently contradictory and misconceived one. In Discount Letter it is clearly stated that this discount offer will continue till execution of the formal contract between the parties.

21. Having regard to the Agreements dated 29-7-2014, DoV dated 16-3-2015 and Assignment agreement dated 11-6-2019 it is crystal clear that the parties voluntarily agreed to contained a forum selection clause invoking non-exclusive Jurisdiction of the Swiss Court to resolve their dispute under the Swiss law. Therefore, the opposite parties cannot express their position in approbate and reprobate way and, as such, they are estoppel from refusing to go for invoking the forum clause.

22. That the opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 filed Counter-Affidavit on 13-2-2020 stating that the cause of action for the proceedings before the Court of Switzerland is clearly different and arising under different agreement (being software Agreement (OT-2014-638 dated 29-7-2014) than the cause of action of the Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 before the Court of Bangladesh which is arising under the Discount Agreement dated 23-6-2014. It is further stated that the present Petitioner was well aware of the conciliation proceedings in Switzerland before filing of the instant revision.

23. We have carefully gone through the respective case of the parties. It appears that the plaintiffs-opposite party No. 1 instituted present Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka Bangladesh on 22-6-2017 stating the cause of action in paragraph No. 16 of the plaint that cause of action of the suit arose on 23-6-2014 when Ziaur Rahman, Chairman of the 1st and 2nd plaintiffs offered discount letter to the defendant for sum 5,000,000 (Five Million).

24. In the Money Suit No 62 of 2017 the plaintiffs-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2 claimed an amount of BDT 10,77,30,845.01 and US $ 3,045,070,77 equivalent to BDT 245,889,465 in total sum of Taka 353,620,319.01. The plaintiffs issued two letters to the defendant-petitioner unilaterally terminating the contracts on 4-8-2016 and 10-8-2016 respectively.

25. Thus from plain reading of the plaint of Money Suit No. 62 of 2017, Supplementary-Affidavit dated 5-2-2020, Counter-Affidavit filed by the opposite parties dated 8-2-2020 and Counter-Affidavit of opposite party No. 1 against the Supplementary-Affidavit of the petitioner dated 5-2-2020, it is crystal clear that primarily plaintiffs filed Money Suit No. 62 of 2017 in the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka against the defendant petitioner on 22-6-2017 claiming a total sum of Taka 353,620,319.01 terminating two contract agreements both dated 29-7-2014 on 4-8-2016 and 10-8-2016. Thereafter, on 21-8-2018 for the same contract Agreements, plaintiff Nos. 1 and 2 invoked jurisdiction of Court of Geneva of Switzerland out of the same cause of action as per Article 9 of the Purchase Agreement (ref OT-2014-928) between the parties.

26. At the very outset, we like to make it clear that the defendant-petitioner filed the application for rejecting the plaint for lack of jurisdiction. In the backdrop of the facts and circumstance of the case, the findings given by the learned Joint District Judge, we shall examine first whether the learned Joint District Judge was right in rejecting the payer for rejection of the plaint on the views that there is no scope to decide whether the Bangladesh Court have jurisdiction to decide this matter before taking evidence and moreover, none of the ingredients of Order VII, rule 11 is available.

27. Let us see whether in the facts and circumstances of the case as disclosed in the plaints as well as in the application, any of the situations as contemplated in Order VII, rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure was attracted warranting rejection of the plaint.

<u>28. In present case, on perusal of the plaint, it clearly shows that facts constituting cause of action have been stated in paragraph No. 16 of the plaint. The only claim of the defendant on which it ought to reject the plaint that the First Joint District Judge, Dhaka, Bangladesh had no jurisdiction/lack of jurisdiction to try the suit against the defendant. Considering the statements made in the plaint as well in the application, it appears to us that none of the situation as contemplated in Order VII, rule 11 of the Code was attracted. It is true that the provisions of rule 11 are not exhaustive in the matter of rejection of plaint and in exceptional situation a plaint can be rejected under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure, even if it does not come within the mischief of the rule, but such situation is absent in the present case.</u>

29. In this revision, Learned Advocate appearing for both the parties made extensive arguments in respect of 'forum selection clause' in the contract Agreement providing for the litigation of any dispute in the competent Courts of Geneva, Switzerland.

30. The petitioners took a preliminary objection that the Joint District Judge First Court Dhaka, Bangladesh had no jurisdiction to entertain the suit as parties by express contract stipulated in Articles 9 and 19 of the Agreements dated 29-7-2014 had agreed to confer exclusive jurisdiction in regard to all disputes arising out of the contract in the competent Court of Geneva, Switzerland.

31. In both the contract Agreements dated 29-7-2014 Articles 19 and 9 speaks of APPLICABLE LAW which runs as follows: "Any dispute arising between the parties over Construction, Validity, Performance, or non-performance or causing of his agreement shall be subject to be sole competence of the competent court of Geneva, Switzerland."

32. Subsequently, Agreements dated 29-7-2014 with the plaintiffs Nos. 1 and 2 was amended by the Deed of Variation (DoV) dated 16-3-2015. JURISDICTION clause 5 and 6 states as below:

6. JURISDICTION Each party irrevocably agrees that the competent courts of Geneva, Switzerland shall have non-exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this deed or its subject matter or formation (including non-contractual disputes or claims).

33. It is true that the learned Joint District Judge can always return the plaint, if the court has no jurisdiction either pecuniary on territorial to entertain the suit. But in the light of the facts of the present case, there is no scope to return the plaint to the plaintiffs since the plaintiffs in their plaint clearly stated that the plaintiffs are the companies, carries its business in Bangladesh and defendant has also a sub-ordinate office in Bangladesh. The plaintiffs are allowed to bring this suit before this court in Bangladesh due to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the court of Geneva, Switzerland under the terms of the Agreement. This court has jurisdiction as the parties, the place of making contract, place of performance and subject matter of the contracts in relation of production and supply of Smart NID Cards to Bangladesh Election Commission (BEC). Since the suit is filed seeking compensation for breach of contract by the defendant in relation to Agreements dated 29-7-2014 as amended by the Deed of Variation (DoV) dated 16-3-2015, therefore, the entire subject matter of the aforesaid contracts arose within the jurisdiction of Bangladesh court and thus the cause of action has arisen in Bangladesh, when the contract is breached and is therefore, the First Joint District Judge, Dhaka Bangladesh has jurisdiction under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure to try the suit.

34. In this connection, both the parties relied on the decision reported in 22 DLR (SC) 334 wherein their Lordships observed that the Pakistan Supreme Court held exclusive jurisdiction clause in the Bill of Leading ousting the jurisdiction of a country's court has to be treated no more than the Exception to section 28 of the Contract Act but it does not take away the Jurisdiction of the Courts of that Country. Parties by contract cannot absolutely oust the Jurisdiction of a court which it has. Such Contract will be hit by the provision of section 28 of the Contract Act.

35. In 17 BLD (AD) 249 = 49 DLR (AD) 187 our Appellate Division in the British Airways case it has been held a civil suit is never intended to be barred in view of existence of arbitration agreement.

36. Apart from the above two decisions, good number of decisions were also cited from Bar on this question of Forum Selection clause in the contract Agreements but those are not necessary for the primary point in issue in the revision.

37. Before parting, it is pertinent to note that explanation of section 10 of the Code of Civil Procedure specifically provides that the pendency of a suit in a foreign court does not preclude the courts in Bangladesh from trying a suit founded on the same cause of action.

38. From the discussion made herein above, we hold the learned Joint District Judge did not commit any error of law in rejecting the application. It is by now a well settled legal preposition that the plaint cannot be rejected on the ground of lack of jurisdiction.

39. In the result the Rule is discharged without any order as to cost. The impugned judgment and order passed by the learned Joint District Judge is affirmed. Order of stay granted at time of issuance of the rule is stands vacated. Send down the Lower Court Records at once. The trial court is directed to proceed with the suit.

Let a copy of the judgment be sent to the concerned court expeditiously.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 01.06.2010, passed by the Single Bench of the High Court Division in Arbitration Application Nos. 02-03 of 2004)
full_judgment:
Mirza Hussain Haider J. These 02 (two) civil petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the judgment and order dated 01.06.2010, passed by a Single Applications being Nos. 02 of 2004 and 03 of 2004, filed under section 42(2) read with section 43 of the Arbitration Act, 2001 (hereinafter referred to as "the Act of 2001") allowing Arbitration Application No. 02 of 2004 filed by present respondent No.1 and rejecting Arbitration Application No. 03 of 2004 filed by the present petitioner and thereby setting aside the award dated 13.05.2004 (as modified by order dated 23.6.2004) passed by the Arbitral Tribunal.

2. Since both the civil petitions arise out of the same judgment and order arising out of same award of the arbitral tribunal and since in both the civil petitions the parties and the facts and circumstances are same, both the civil petitions are taken up together and disposed of by this single judgment.

3. Common facts leading to filing of these two civil petitions for leave to appeal in short are:

<u>4. That the present respondent No.1, Startus Construction Company (hereinafter referred to as "the company") entered into a contract with the Roads and Highways Department, Government of the People's Republic of Bangladesh (hereinafter referred to as "the Department") for construction/rehabilitation of Roads and Highways between joydebpur and Kaliakair measuring approximately 26.60 km. After observing necessary formalities, the company started the work under the contract and duly completed part of the work upto 5.0 km. However, while undertaking the work for the first aforesaid 5.0 km. of the project, the company started facing certain obstacles with regard to underground gas pipe lines and as such requested the Department to take necessary steps for removal of the said gas pipe lines so that the company can undertake and complete the project work without any hindrarice. Although the department assured to do the same, but ultimately the matter was not resolved and at one stage, the project work was suspended without any fault on the part of the company. Then both the parties engaged in discussions and also exchanged correspondences, which also involved various other Ministry/Departments of the Government.</u>

5. Eventually, there being no further progress in the matter, the work came to standstill and as such, the company issued notice dated 14.8.2001 claiming compensation with a request to return the bank guarantee, which was furnished earlier by it. Subsequently, the company served a notice on 20.8.2001 for resolving the matter by Arbitration. On the other hand, the Department by its letter dated 16.08.2001, approved various orders and voluntarily extended the contract period upto 06.05.2002, but, after three days, the Department ultimately terminated the contract by its letter dated 19.08.2001.

6. Thereafter as per agreement, the dispute between the parties was referred to a three member Arbitration Tribunal, comprising of Mr. Justice Sultan Hossain Khan as the Chairman and Mr. Justice M.A. Karim and Mr. Justice M.M. Hoque as the other two members of the said arbitral tribunal. Therein against the statement of claim filed by the company the Department duly entered appearance and participated in the proceedings, without filing any counter claim. It simply filed its statement of defence.

7. For resolving the disputes between the parties, the tribunal framed the following issues:

"(1) Has the employer committed breach of contract in not removing the gas pipeline and thus prevented SCC (i.e. the company) from performing the latter's promise? (2) Has the claimant sustained any loss in consequence of its non-performance of the contract? If so, what compensation the company is entitled to? (3) Is the certification of default of the contractor issued by the Engineer baseless and illegal? (4) Is the contract liable to be terminated at the instance of SCC in view of section 53 of the Contract Act.? (5) Has the termination of the contract by the Employer been legal and valid? (6) Has the valuation of the variations by the engineer been legal and valid? (7) Is the claimant entitled to get the award as prayed for including the additional claim against bitumen and cost of the proceeding?"

8. Upon hearing the parties and considering the materials on record, the tribunal by order dated 13.05.2004, dismissed the claim of the company and made an award of TK.6,25,46,127.66(Taka six crore twenty five lac forty six thousand one hundred and twenty seven and sixty six paisa) only in favour of the Department. The tribunal also directed to release the bank guarantee in favour of the company.

9. Thereafter, the company filed an application for correction of the award dated 13.5.2004 which was allowed by the tribunal by its order dated 23.6.2004 and the award was corrected by reducing the amount to TK.3,29,82,629.56(Taka three crore twenty nine lac eighty two thousand six hundred twenty nine and paisa fifty six) only.

10. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid Award dated 13.05.2004(as amended by order dated 23.6.2004), the company moved the High Court Division in Arbitration Application No. 02 of 2004 under section 42(2) read with section 43(i)(a)(iv) of the Arbitration Act, 2001, for setting aside the Award. At the same time, the Department also filed Arbitration Application No. 03 of 2004 for correction of the Award by setting aside the portion of the award dated 13.5.2004(as amended by order dated 23.6.2004), particularly in paragraphs Nos. 18.6, 18.7, 18.8, 18.9, 22, 24, 25.4, 26 and 27 of the Award and thereby prayed for passing a corrected award as per prayers made in Prayers "A to E" of paragraph 7 of the application.

<u>11. The High Court Division, upon hearing the parties and on perusal of the materials on record, allowed Arbitration Application No. 02 of 2004 filed by the company on setting aside the award dated 13.5.2004(as amended by order dated 23.6.2004) and dismissed Arbitration Application No. 03 of 2004 filed by the department, by the impugned judgment and order dated 01.06.2010.</u>

<u>12. Hence the Roads and Highways Department, Roads Division, moved this Division in the aforesaid two civil petitions for redress.</u>

13. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, the learned Attorney General appearing on behalf of the leave-petitioner in both the civil petitions, submits that the High Court Division erred both in law and in fact while passing the impugned judgment and order in setting aside the award without considering that the award does not call for any interference from the Court save and except to the extent to which it relates to the issues not submitted to the arbitral tribunal and as such the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. Mr. Alam submits that the Court has ample power under sections 42 and 43(1) (i) (a) (iv) of the Act of 2001 to separate the award from the issues which were not submitted before the arbitral tribunal and accordingly set aside that portion of the award so far it relates to the matter not referred to the arbitral tribunal. In elaborating his submission the learned Attorney General contended that although the claimant company did not refer to certain disputes/issues such as claim for refund against bitumen, retention of money, reduction of VAT or its return in favour of the company as well as return of the Bank Guarantee submitted by the company, but the arbitral tribunal erred in law by travelling beyond its jurisdiction in allowing the same in favour of the claimant company and as such the High Court Division had ample opportunity to correct and modify the award in accordance with law in Arbitration Application No. 03 of 2004 but in not doing so the High Court Division committed illegality in passing the judgment which is required to be interfered with by this Division.

14. Dr. Sharif Mohammad Nur Ullah Bhuiyan, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the respondent-company by filing caveat in both. the civil petitions submits that in the arbitration proceeding, the claimant company submitted its statement of claim for an amount of TK.11 crore and odd while the Department i.e. the present petitioner did not file/submit any counter claim, but the arbitral tribunal dismissed the claim of the claimant company and passed an award amounting to TK. 6 crore and odd(which has been reduced to TK.3 crore and odd) in favour of the Department i.e. the present petitioner and as such, it is clear that the arbitral tribunal travelled beyond the terms of reference made to it by the parties under the contract and thus it acted beyond its jurisdiction in passing the award in favour of the Department and as such the High Court Division rightly appreciated the matter and set aside the award by the impugned judgment and order in accordance with law which is liable to be affirmed by this Division.

15. On hearing the learned Advocates for both the parties and on perusal of the materials on record as well as the impugned judgment and order, it appears that the main point for determination in these two civil petitions is whether the arbitral tribunal had jurisdiction to give the alleged award in favour of the Department when admittedly no counter claim has been made by the Department and the issues for passing such award had not been referred to by the Department to the tribunal. The principle of law in respect of arbitration is that the tribunal is to decide only such issues as are referred to it by the parties to the proceedings. In fact the power of the arbitral tribunal is confined within the terms of reference made to it by the parties under the con-tract. Under such circumstances, any deviation therefrom enables the parties to invoke/raise the question of jurisdiction of the tribunal.

16. The point as raised herein has categorically been dealt with by the High Court Division while passing the judgment and order impugned herein.

17. In respect of the submission of the learned Advocate for the respondent company that 'the tribunal has travelled beyond its jurisdiction by deciding the issues which were not referred to it', the High Court Division evidently found support from the affidavit-in-opposition dated 01.011.2009 filed by the Department (the present petitioner) wherein in paragraph-4, it has been stated as under:

"The calculation made under the heading "Final Position" is not an out-come of any counter claim made by the respondent rather it is outcome of an unwarranted arithmetic calculation made by the Tribunal on the basis of its discussion on the valid as well as invalid determinable disputes and Annexure 17 to the Award submitted by the claimant/petitioner before the Tribunal. The calculation under the head "Final Position" is not consequential of the adjudication of 3(three) valid referred disputes under clause 67 of GCOC. The said calculation therefore is not relatable to the three valid referred disputes under clause 67 of GCOC. The final position is therefore relatable to issue, which were not referred to arbitration as dispute following the mechanism/ procedure under clause 67 of GCOC. The "Final Position" is extraneous to the 3(three) valid referred disputes."

18. The aforesaid statement made in the affidavit in opposition filed by the Department has been corroborated by the tribunal while passing the award in question wherein it has observed as under:

"We have noticed that the respondent had claimed various amounts as shown by way of submissions of summary of additional, cost and amount due from the Contractor. These claims were not referred to the Arbitrators in terms of Clause 67 of the Contract. The calculation therefore is not relatable to the three valid referred disputes under clause 67 of GCOC."

19. Moreover, the same also finds support in the dissenting view of the Award dated 13.5.2004 passed by one of the Arbitrators (Mr. Justice M.M. Haque) where he observed:

"It may be mentioned here that there is no counter claim by the said respondent …)".

<u>20. Accordingly, the High Court Division held "no counter claim was filed by the Roads and Highways Department, but the Tribunal nevertheless proceeded to make an Award in their favour which was beyond their terms 4o.f reference. It is also admitted by Mr. Ariff, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Roads and Highways Department that only three disputes were referred to the Tribunal and upon commencement of the proceeding, the Tribunal framed as many as seven issues, as has been quoted earlier. However, from a reading of the same, it does not appear that it relates to any counter claim filed by the Department."</u>

<u>21. In coming to the conclusion, on the issue of jurisdiction of the tribunal, the High Court Division relied upon the decisions in the case of West Bengal Industrial Infrastructure Development Corporation Vs. M/s. Star Engineering Co. reported in AIR 1987 (Cal) 126 which arises out of similar facts and circumstances as of the present case. In the aforesaid case also no counter claim was filed but the tribunal adjudicated the issue on an imaginary counter claim. Hence in the aforesaid reported case, it has been held:</u>

<u>"In my opinion, this gross mistakes has arisen from culpable negligence amounting to legal misconduct in the part of the arbitrator in making the Award and as such this Award cannot be upheld."</u>

22. The High Court Division also relied on the case of Chetandas and others Vs. Radhakrisson Ramchandra and others reported in AIR 1921 Bombay 553 where-in it has been held:

"In cases where an arbitrator enters into the consideration of matters which are not referred to him, or which he has no jurisdiction to try, Blackburn, J. in Ringland Vs. Lowndes (1) (1864) 12 W.R. 1010) said that the question is not one of the waiver or of estoppels, but of authority, and a party continuing to attend the reference after objection taken and protest made does not give the arbitrator authority to make an award. Even if a party under protest continues to attend before arbitrators and cross examines witnesses, he does not thereby waive his objection, nor is he stopped from saying that the arbitrators have exceeded their authority by awarding on the matter."

23. In this respect the submission advanced on behalf of the Department on section 43(1)(a)(iv) of the Act, the High Court Division found that 'the award which has been passed in the instant case stands embodied under the head "Final Position" as contained at page 58 of the Award, whereby an Award of Taka six crores and odd(which was subsequently reduced to Taka three crores and odd by order dated 23.6.2004) was made in favour of the Roads and Highways Department, despite the absence of any counter claim filed on their behalf (underlined for emphasis) which has been corroborated in their own affidavit in opposition dated 01.11.2009. Therefore, The High Court Division held "it would become difficult, if not impossible, to sever the determinable issues from the non determinable issues referred to the tribunal from the final award which is not before the Court."

24. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case and the decisions referred to above, the High Court Division finally held that "having regard to the statements made in the application before this Court, the relevant provisions of law, the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates for the contending sides and last, but not least, having considered the decisions referred to above, with which I find myself in total and respectful agreement, I am inclined to hold that the Arbitral tribunal travelled beyond its jurisdiction by entertaining and deciding issues which has not been referred to by the contending sides and the impugned order is liable to be set aside."

<u>25. The aforesaid findings and decision arrived at by the High Court Division being fully based on proper appreciation of the fact and law as well as the decisions referred to above, the same does not suffer from any material or legal infirmity. Because the arbitration tribunal derives its jurisdiction on and from the matter and issues referred to it by the parties to the arbitration. It has no power of its own to decide any matter which is not referred to it or which has no basis in their respective claims or counter claim, if any. When there is no counter claim made by the other party it clearly Prolits that it does not have any claim of its own rather it simply defends itself against the genuineness of the claim of the claimant. And when no such counter claim is being made the tribunal has the jurisdiction only to see whether the claim of the claimant is genuine/proved and can decide the matter only to the said extent and not beyond that, not to speak of giving award which has not been sought for by the other party to the arbitration. If it does so, then the same will be completely beyond the jurisdiction. Jurisdiction goes to the root of the matter and if any order is passed by any authority without having jurisdiction such order/award will have no other fate but to be dismissed or shall become an illegal order/award for want of jurisdiction.</u>

<u>26. Moreover, from the issues framed for determination by the arbitral tribunal it appears that no such issue was Aframed to determine whether the Department would get anything because it made no counter claim against the clamant company. Since there was no counter claim the tribunal rightly did not frame any issue on it. But in passing an award of taka six crores and odd or the reduced amount of taka three crores and odd in favour of the Department the tribunal has travelled beyond the terms of reference and as such, the same is beyond its jurisdiction.</u>

<u>27. Thus, it is held that the High Court Division did not commit any illegality in setting aside the award on the ground of lack of jurisdiction. Thus, we do not find any reason to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.</u>

<u>28. Accordingly, both the civil petitions for leave to appeal are dismissed without any order as to costs.</u>

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 30.01.2019 and 03.02.2019 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 13989 of 2016)
full_judgment:
Zinat Ara J. This Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 3039 of 2019 is directed against the judgment and order dated 30.01.2019 and 03.02.2019 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 13989 of 2016 making the rule absolute with certain declarations and directions.

Writ Petitioner- HRPB- Respondent No.1's Case

<u>2. Writ Petitioner- Human Rights and Peace for Bangladesh (shortly, HRPB) filed Writ Petition No. 13989 of 2016 against Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Shipping; Chairman, Bangladesh Inland Water Transport Authority (BIWTA); Director General, Department of Environment; Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur and others contending, inter alia, that HRPB is a non-profitable registered organization. The objects of this organization are to uphold the human rights of the citizen, to work for the poor people, to give legal support to the helpless people, etc. HRPB also works to protect the environment as well as health and hygiene of the citizen. HRPB filed the writ petition under article 102 of the Constitution as a Public Interest Litigation in order to take necessary steps to stop earth filling and encroachment within the territory of Turag river. On 06.11.2016, a report was published in "The Daily Star" on Turag river with the caption/title: "Time to declare Turag dead: River grabbers appear mightier than Government, Judiciary; all steps go in vain." Along with the report, "The Daily Star" publishes cozens of satellite images/photographs taken between the years 2013 to 2016 relating to encroachments of Turag river by earth filling, making constructions, etc. The report also contained some highlights of river grabbing and encroachments and earth filling at Kamarpara Bridge at Tongi, Birulia near Mirpur embankment, Dhour Bridge in Bhadam Mouza, etc. According to the report, grabbers occupied Turag river and its foreshore following the incorrectly placed demarcation pillars by the authorities concerned. The newspaper report also revealed that Turag river at the north of Birulia Bridge is now merely 100 feet in width. All the grabbing and encroachment by earth filling, etc. of river Turag are being held before the local administration and concerned authorities, but proper steps are not being taken for saving Turag. A river is a source of water, fishes, river communication and a good harvest as well. Turag has influenced and contributed to the livelihood of the citizens of Dhaka and Gazipur for many years. Now it has become practically a dead river due to grabbing of the river with its foreshore lands by earth filling and illegal encroachment at different places. Due to continuous encroachment and earth filling of the width/navigability affecting the life of the citizens at large. Such encroachment has a serious negative environmental impact on the nearby areas and areas beside Turag affecting adversely the livelihood and health and hygiene of the citizens. The illegal encroachment has been increasing day by day by establishing illegal projects, factories and homestead within Turag river territory. The main cause of environmental degradation is unauthorized filling up of the river around the country. Such encroachment by earth filling, establishing factories and other projects are violative of the provisions of several laws of the land. Previously in order to protect the rivers, namely, Buriganga, Turag, Balu, Shitalakshya, etc. HRPB had filed a writ petition. In the said case of HRPB and others Vs. Bangladesh and others reported in 14 BLC (HCD) (2009) 759, the Supreme Court of Bangladesh has delineated detailed measures to recover the ailing rivers from the river/land grabbers and save the rivers from pollution. But the river and land grabbers are violating the verdict of the Court as well as the laws of the land in collusion of some officials of the concerned authorities, who are responsible for protecting the river.</u>

<u>3. In the backdrop of aforesaid facts and circumstances, HRPB filed the writ petition for direction upon the respondents to remove all earth filling and structures from Turag river territory at the cost of the encroachers, to direct respondent No. 6 to submit a report within 3(three) weeks mentioning the names and addresses of the persons and companies making construction by encroaching upon Turag river, Gazipur and also to direct respondent Nos. 2, 4 and 9 to take steps to stop all kinds of earth filling, encroachments and construction within Turag river territory and to submit compliance report and obtained the rule.</u>

4. On 09.11.2016, the respondents were directed by the High Court Division to comply with the direction given by the Court in Writ Petition No. 3503 of 2009, so far as it relates to eviction of unauthorized encroachers of Turag river. Thereafter, BIWTA after eviction of some encroachers submitted a report on 05.01.2017. During hearing, it was found that some of the unauthorized occupants were not evicted from their illegal occupation by demolishing the illegal structures. Therefore, actual scenario relating to the encroachment of Turag river with the names of encroachers and structures thereon were necessary. In such situation, the High Court Division passed over in Writ Petition No. 13989 of 2016 on 05.01.2017 to ascertain the actual position of Turag through judicial inquiry.

5. Mr. Mohammad Asshams Joglul Hossain, Judicial Inquiry Officer as well as Chief Judicial Magistrate, Gazipur made a thorough investigation/inquiry relating to illegal encroachment of Turag river at Gazipur and submitted a detailed report on 11.10.2017 with some recommendations. On 02.12.2017, he also asked the Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur, Superintendent of Police, Gazipur, BIWTA and all other concerned authorities to assist the Chief Judicial Magistrate for eviction of the unauthorized occupants from the territory of Turag river.

Affidavits-in-Opposition

6. Respondent Nos. 10-23, unauthorized occupants of Turag river as per judicial inquiry report, were added as respondents in the writ petition and the said respondents as well as some other respondents contested the rule by submitting separate Affidavits-in-Opposition.

7. Respondent No. 10 Dhaka Central International Medical College Hospital (CIMCH) in its Affidavit-in-Opposition contended that it has purchased the land as mentioned in the judicial inquiry report in the year 2012-2013 and also mutated its name; that pillars were correctly setup by the concerned authorities as per direction in Writ Petition No. 3503 of 2009; that its property is outside the said boundary pillar and not within the boundary of the river and its offshore lands; that the Chief Judicial Magistrate during his inquiry did not allow him to place his case; that CIMCH has been evicted from the river land as per direction of the Court.

8. Added respondent No. 12 Nishat Jute Mills Limited (hereinafter mentioned as Nishat) represented by Abul Kalam Azad, in its Affidavit-in-Opposition denied the averments made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that Nishat Jute Mills Limited was purchased by the present management from Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation through tender notice. Nishat Jute Mills was a Mill under Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation. After sale the Government handed over possession of the said 22.90 acres of land in favour of the purchaser after due survey. According to the report of the Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur, the land shown to have been encroached upon by the purchaser of Nishat in the judicial inquiry report is the land of Nishat. Writ Petition No. 13989 of 2016 is not maintainable as the writ-petitioner previously filed Writ Petition No. 3503 of 2009 over the same subject. The purchaser of Nishat Jute Mills Limited filed a written objection against judicial inquiry report and claimed that the judicial inquiry report was done beyond the knowledge of Nishat and, as such, it was deprived of fair justice.

9. Respondent Nos. 13-21 in their Affidavits-in-Opposition stated that they have not constructed any structure within the boundary of Turag river. Rather, they by purchase of their respective lands from C.S, S.A and R.S recorded owners/their heirs became the owners of the said land and have been in possession thereof by constructing houses on the said lands. At the time of demarcation of the river in compliance with the direction of the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3503 of 2009, pillars were correctly setup and after the pillars, walkway/pavement was constructed and trees were planted by the concerned authorities. In the said judgment, BIWTA was directed to take possession from high water mark of the river. But the high water mark was relating to Port area only and not the entire river. The rest of the area was according to the C.S survey. The Chief Judicial as offshore land of Turag, although their construction did not cross the C.S boundary of Turag.

10. All the contesting respondents claimed that the report of the Chief Judicial Magistrate is hypothetical, erroneous and the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division on the basis of the said investigation/inquiry report is erroneous, unlawful and thus, liable to be set aside.

Decision of the High Court Division

11. The High Court Division upon hearing the arguments of the contending parties made the Rule absolute and the Court decided,

“যেহেতু ১২ নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষকে প্রদত্ত লীজ দলিলের তফসিল সংশ্লিষ্ট জমি পাবলিক ট্রাস্ট সম্পত্তি তথা জনগণের সম্পত্তি অর্থাৎ রাষ্ট্র উক্ত সম্পত্তির মালিক নন শুধুমাত্র ট্রাস্টি তথা আমানত গ্রহীতা, সেহেতু সরকার কর্তৃক ১২নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষকে প্রদত্ত পাবলিক ট্রাস্ট সম্পত্তির (Public Trust Property) হস্তান্তর দলিল বা লীজ দলিল একটি বেআইনী দলিল। অর্থাৎ দলিলটির সৃষ্টিই হয়েছে পাবলিক ট্রাস্ট মতবাদের পরিপন্থীভাবে তথা সংবিধান পরিপন্থীভাবে তথা বেআইনীভাবে।সেহেতু এটি ছিল শুরুতেই বাতিল একটি দলিল তথা

void ab initio | যে দলিলটি শুরুতেই বাতিল দলিল তার উপর ভিত্তি করে ১২নং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ

কোন প্রতিকার পেতে পারে না।”

[vide page 59 of the judgment]

12. The High Court Division also passed judgment and order with the following declarations and directions:

“অবৈধ দূষণ ও দখল এবং মাটি ভরাট হতে তুরাগ নদীকে রক্ষা করতে প্রতিবাদী পক্ষগণের “নিষ্ক্রিয়তা” আইনসংগত কর্তৃত্ব ব্যতিরেকে গ্রহণ করা হয়েছে বিধায় উক্ত নিষ্ক্রিয়তার কোন আইনগত কার্যকারিতা নাই মর্মে ঘোষণা করা হল এবং তুরাগ নদীতে অবৈধভাবে সংঘটিত দূষণ ভরাটকৃত মাটি এবং নির্মিত স্থাপনাদি দখলদারদের খরচে উত্তোলন আইনের দ্বারা প্রতিবাদীপক্ষগণের করণীয় কার্য হেতু নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো। আমরা, অতঃপর, নিম্নেবর্ণিত আদেশ এবং নির্দেশনাসমূহ প্রদান করলামঃ

১। অত্র রায়ে যে পাবলিক ট্রাষ্ট মতবাদ (Public Trust Doctrine)এর বিশদ ব্যাখ্যা, বিশ্লেষণ এবং বর্ণনা করা হলো তা আমাদের দেশের আইনের অংশ।

২। “তুরাগ নদীকে আইনি ব্যক্তি (Legal Person) আইনি সত্তা(legal entity) জীবন্ত সত্তা(living entity) ঘোষনা করা হল। বাংলাদেশের মধ্যে এবং বাংলাদেশের মধ্য দিয়ে প্রবাহমান সকল নদ-নদী একই মর্যাদা পাবে।

৩। নদী রক্ষা কমিশন'-কে তুরাগ নদীসহ দেশের সকল নদ-নদী দূষণ ও দখলমুক্ত করে সুরক্ষা, সংরক্ষণ এবং উন্নয়নের নিমিত্ত আইনগত অভিভাবক (person inloco parentis) Caan করা হল।

নদ-নদী সংশ্লিষ্ট সকল সংস্থা, অধিদপ্তর এবং মন্ত্রণালয়ের সহযোগীতায়, অদ্য হতে বাংলাদেশের সকল নদ-নদীর দূষণ ও দখলমুক্ত করে স্বাভাবিক নৌ চলাচলের উপযোগী করে সুরক্ষা, সংরক্ষণ, উন্নয়ন, শ্রীবৃদ্ধিসহ যাবতীয় উন্নয়নে জাতীয় নদী রক্ষা কমিশন বাধ্য থাকিবে। নদনদী সংশ্লিষ্ট সকল সংস্থা, অধিদপ্তর এবং মন্ত্রণালয় এ ব্যাপারে নদী কমিশনকে সঠিক এবং যথাযথ সাহায্য ও সহযোগীতা দিতে বাধ্য থাকবে।

৪। আগাম প্রতিরোধের নীতি (The Precautionary Principle)এবং দুষণকারী কর্তৃক ক্ষতিপূরণ প্রদানের নীতি (Polluter’s Pay Principle) আমাদের দেশের আইনের অংশ হিসেবে ঘোষণা করা হল।

৫। তুরাগ নদী সহ দেশের সকল নদ নদী খাল বিল জলাশয়ের ক্ষেত্রে নতুন প্রকল্প প্রণয়নের লক্ষ্যে পরিকল্পনা কমিশন, এলজিইডি, পানি উন্নয়ন বোর্ড, বিআইডব্লিউ, বিএডিসি সহ সকল সংস্থা জাতীয় নদী রক্ষা কমিশনকে অবহিত করবেন এবং জাতীয় নদী রক্ষা কমিশনের অনাপত্তিপত্র গ্রহণ করবেন।

৬। ১০ থেকে ২৩ নং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ আগামী ৩০(ত্রিশ) দিনের মধ্যে সংশ্লিষ্ট নদীর অবৈধ দখল থেকে নিজেদেরকে সরিয়ে নেবেন । অন্যথায় জাতীয় নদী রক্ষা কমিশন সংশিষ্ট কর্তৃপক্ষের সহযোগিতায় ১০ থেকে ২৩ নং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষের খরচে তাদেরকে উচ্ছেদ করবে । নদী দখলকারী দখল উচ্ছেদের এবং যাবতীয় খরচ বহন করবে ।

৭। নদী দখলকে এবং নদী দূষণকে ফৌজদারী অপরাধ গণ্য করে এর কঠিন সাজা এবং বড় আকারের জরিমানা নির্ধারণ করতঃ এবং এই সংক্রান্তে মামলা দায়ের, তদন্ত এবং বিচারের পদ্ধতি ২০১৩ এর প্রয়োজনীয় সংশোধনের উদ্যোগ গ্রহণ করতঃ এবং এতদবিষয় কি পদক্ষেপ ১ নং প্রতিপক্ষ গ্রহণ করেছে তদবিষয়ে আগামী ৬ মাসের মধ্যে অত্র বিভাগে হলফনামা সম্পাদনের মাধ্যমে অবহিত করার জন্য ১নং প্রতিপক্ষকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো।

৮। ডিজিটাল ডাটাবেজ প্রণয়নের ক্ষেত্রে এসপিএ, আরআর এসও সেটেলাইটের সাহায্যে আরএস/জিআইএস উন্নত প্রযুক্তি ব্যবহারের মাধ্যমে বাংলাদেশের সকল নদ নদী খাল বিল জলাশয়ের ভৌগলিক অবস্থান নির্ণয় এবং জীব বৈচিত্র বিষয়ক তথ্যাদি সংগ্রহপূর্বক সকল ইউনিয়ন, উপজেলা এবং জেলার ম্যাপ প্রস্তুত করতঃ সংশ্লিষ্ট স্ব স্ব দপ্তর সকল নাগরিকের জন্য উন্মুক্ত স্থানে বিলবোর্ড আকারে প্রদর্শন করবে এবং যেকোন নাগরিক নির্ধারিত ফিসের বিনিময়ে যেন উক্ত ডাটাবেজ বা ম্যাপ সংগ্রহ করতে পারে সে ব্যাপারে সংশ্লিষ্ট উপজেলা এবং জেলা প্রশাসন এর কার্যালয় প্রয়ণাজনীয় পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণ করবেন।

৯। জাতীয় নদী রক্ষা কমিশনকে একটি কার্যকরি স্বাধীন প্রতিষ্ঠানে পরিণত করার নিমিত্ত ১ নং প্রতিপক্ষকে প্রয়োজনীয় সকল পদক্ষেপ অনতিবিলম্বে গ্রহণ করার নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো ।

১০। বাংলাদেশের সকল সরকারী বেসরকারী স্কুল, স্কুল এন্ড কলেজ, কলেজ, মাদ্রাসা, কারিগরি শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান এবং সরকারী বেসরকারী সকল, বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের প্রতিটি শ্রেণিতে এবং বিভাগে প্রতি দুই মাস অন্তর একদিন এক ঘন্টার একটি নদীর প্রয়োজনীয়তা, উপকারিতা, রক্ষা, দূষণ সংরক্ষণ বিষয়ে সচেতনতামূলক ক্লাস পরিচালনা এবং প্রতিটি শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান স্ব স্ব এলাকার ভিতর দিয়ে প্রবাহিত নদী নিয়মিতভাবে পরিদর্শনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করবে । এছাড়াও প্রতিটি শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠানে বড় পর্দায় নদী, প্রকৃতি ও পরিবেশ এর উপর দেশী-বিদেশী ডকুমেন্টারী ছবি প্রদর্শনের ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণের নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো। এবং এতদবিষয়ে সকল শিক্ষা প্রতিষ্ঠান নির্দেশ মোতাবেক ক্লাস নিচ্ছে কিনা তা তদারকী করার জন্য শিক্ষা মন্ত্রনালয়কে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো।

১১। ছোট বড় মাঝারি বৃহদাকার সকল দেশী বিদেশী সরকারী বেসরকারী শিল্প কারখানাসমূহকে তাদের সকল শ্রমিকদের অংশগ্রহণে প্রতি দুইমাস অন্তর একদিন এক ঘন্টার একটি নদী বিষয়ক ‘বৈঠক অনুষ্ঠানের নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো। এতদবিষয়ে সকল শিল্প কারখানা নির্দেশ মোতাবেক নদী বিষয়ক বৈঠক করেছে কিনা তা তদারকি করার জন্য শিল্প মন্ত্রণালয়কে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো।

১২। দেশের প্রতিটি ইউনিয়ন, উপজেলা, পৌরসভা এবং জেলায় প্রতি তিন মাস অন্তর একদিন দিনব্যাপী প্রতিযোগীতা, আলোচনা এবং সেমিনার করার জন্য সকল ইউনিয়ন পরিষদের চেয়ারম্যান, উপজেলার চেয়ারম্যান, পৌর মেয়র এবং জেলা পরিষদের চেয়ারম্যানকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো ।

১৩। দেশের প্রতিটি ইউনিয়ন, উপজেলা, পৌরসভা এবং জেলার অন্তর্গত সকল নদ-নদী দখলদার এবং দুষণকারী ব্যক্তি, প্রতিষ্ঠান এর নামের তালিকা প্রস্তুত করতঃ আগামী ৬ মাসের মধ্যে সংশিষ্ট ইউনিয়ন পরিষদ, উপজেলা পরিষদ, পৌরসভা এবং জেলা কার্যালয়ের নোটিশ বোর্ডে জনসাধারণের অবগতির জন্য উন্মুক্ত স্থানে বিলবোর্ড আকারে টাঙ্গানোর জন্য সকল ইউনিয়ন ও উপজেলা পরিষদের চেয়ারম্যান এবং জেলা প্রশাসককে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হল।

১৪। যেহেতু পরিবেশ, জলবায়ু, জলাভূমি, তথা সমুদ্র, সমুদ্র সৈকত, নদনদী, নদ-নদীর পাড়, খাল-বিল, হাওর-বাওর, নালা, ঝিল, বিরি এবং সকল উন্মুক্ত জলাভূমি, পাহাড়-পর্বত, বন, বন্যপ্রাণী এবং বাতাস যেহেতু পাবলিক ট্রাষ্ট সম্পত্তি (Public Trust Property) তথা জনগণের ন্যাস সম্পত্তি তথা জাতীয় সম্পত্তি (Public Property) সেহেতু উক্ত ভূমি দখলের এবং দূষণের অভিযোগ কোন ব্যক্তি বা কোম্পানী বা প্রতিষ্ঠানের বিরুদ্ধে থাকলে উক্ত ব্যক্তি বা কোম্পানী বা প্রতিষ্ঠান সকল প্রকার ব্যাংক ঋণের অযোগ্য মর্মে বাংলাদেশের তফসিলি সকল ব্যাংককে প্রয়োজনীয় নির্দেশনা প্রদান করে সার্কুলার ইস্যু করার জন্য বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংককে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা গেল। আগামী ৬ মাসের মধ্যে নির্দেশনা বাস্তবায়নের অগ্রগতি হলফনামা সম্পাদনের মাধ্যমে অত্র বিভাগকে অবহিত করার জন্য গভর্নর, বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংককে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা গেল।

১৫। যেহেতু পরিবেশ, জলবায়ু, জলাভূমি, তথা বিল, হাওর-বাওর, নালা, ঝিল, ঝিরি এবং সকল উন্মুক্ত জলাভূমি, পাহাড়-পর্বত, বন, বন্যপ্রাণী এবং বাতাস যেহেতু পাবলিক ট্রাষ্ট সম্পত্তি (Public Trust Property) তথা জনগণের ন্যাস সম্পত্তি তথা জাতীয় সম্পত্তি (Public Property) সেহেতু উক্ত সম্পত্তি দখলকার এবং দূষণকারী হিসেবে অভিযুক্ত ব্যক্তিকে বাংলাদেশের সকল ইউনিয়ন, উপজেলা, পৌরসভা, জেলা পরিষদ এবং জাতীয় সংসদ নির্বাচনে প্রার্থীর অযোগ্যতা হিসেবে অন্তর্ভুক্ত করে আগামী ৬ মাসের মধ্যে অত্র বিভাগকে হলফনামা সম্পাদনের মাধ্যমে অবহিত করণের জন্য নির্বাচন কমিশনকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হল।

১৬। নদী বিষয়ে সচেতনতা বৃদ্ধির লক্ষ্যে স্কুল, কলেজ এবং বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের পাঠ্যক্রমে নদ-নদী সংরক্ষণ এবং দূষণ বিষয় অন্তর্ভূক্ত করার জন্য সচিব, শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়কে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো ।

১৭। নদী, প্রকৃতি এবং পরিবেশের উপর নির্মিত দেশ বিদেশের ডকুমেন্টারী ফিল্ম বাংলাদেশ টেলিভিশনে প্রতি শুক্রবার ১ ঘন্টার ১টি পর্ব সম্প্রচার করার জন্য মহাপরিচালক বাংলাদেশ টেলিভিশন-কে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা গেল। এছাড়াও নদী, প্রকৃতি এবং পরিবেশের উপর নির্মিত সপ্তাহে অন্তত ১ দিন ১ ঘন্টার একটি ডকুমেন্টারী ফিল্ম নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো। অত্র রীট মোকদ্দমাটি একটি চলমান আদেশ (Continuing Mandamus) হিসেবি অব্যাহত থাকবে । আরও আদেশ হয় যে, অত্র রীট মোকদ্দমায় প্রদত্ত বিভিন্ন নির্দেশনা সম্পর্কে সংশয়ের উদ্বেক হলে দরখাস্তকারী, প্রতিবাদীগণ, জাতীয় নদী রক্ষা কমিশন, নির্বাচন কমিশন, বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক, শ্রম মন্ত্রণালয়, শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়সহ যে কোন মন্ত্রণালয়, সংস্থা, সরকারী-বেসরকারী প্রতিষ্ঠান বাংলাদেশের সকল নাগরিক হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে নির্দেশনা প্রার্থনা করে আবেদন বা দরখাস্ত দাখিল করতে পারবেন। দরখাস্তকারীর এ্যাডভোকেট মনজিল মোরসেদ সংগে এ্যাউভোকেট মোঃ ছারওয়ার আহাদ চৌধুরি, এ্যাডভোকেট একলাছ উদ্দিন ভুইয়া, এ্যাডভোকেট রিপন বাড়ৈ এবং এ্যাডভোকেট সঞ্জয় মন্ডল সহ সকল প্রতিবাদী পক্ষের এ্যাডভোকেট সৈয়দ মফিজুর রহমান (২নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে), এ্যাডভোকেট মোঃ ইমাম হাসান সংগে এ্যাডভোকেট মোঃ শাহিনুল ইসলাম (৩নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে), এ্যাডভোকেট খন্দকার শাহরিয়ার শাকির (৪ নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে), এ্যাউভোকেট মোঃ হারুন-অররশিদ (১০ নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে), এ্যাডভোকেট মোঃ আসাদুজ্জামান (১২ নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে), এ্যাডভোকেট এ,এম মাহবুব উদ্দিন সংগে এ্যাডভোকেট সাকিব মাহবুব (১৩-২১ নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে), এ্যাডভোকেট মোহাম্মদ মেহেদী হাসান চৌধুরী সংগে এ্যাডভোকেট শেখ ফজলে নূর তাপস, এ্যাডভোকেট অপুর্ব কুমার বিশ্বাস, এ্যাডভোকেট জুসনা পারভীন, এ্যাডভোকেট উপমা বিশ্বাস, এ্যাডভোকেট সপিল ভট্টাচারিয়া (২২-২৩ নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে), এ্যাডভোকেট মোঃ ইকরামুল হক, ডেপুটি এটর্নী জেনারেল সংগে এ্যাডভোকেট পুরবী রানী শর্মা, সহকারী এটর্নী জেনারেল এ্যাডভোকেট পুরবী সাহা, সহকারী এটর্নী জেনারেল ৫(নং প্রতিপক্ষ পক্ষে) অত্র মোকদামায় আদালতকে সহায়তা প্রদান করার জন্য ধন্যবাদ প্রদান করা হলো।

তুরাগ নদীর অবৈধ স্থাপনা চিহ্নিতকরণ সম্পর্কিত বিচার বিভাগীয় তদন্ত কর্মকর্তা ও চীফ জুডিসিয়াল ম্যাজিস্ট্রেট, গাজীপুর জনাব মোহাম্মদ আসসামছ জগলুল হোসেন এবং তাকে সহযোগিতাকারী সকল সরকারী-বেসরকারী কর্মকতা কর্মচারী ও ব্যক্তিগণকে বিশেষ ধন্যবাদ জ্ঞাপন করা হলো। তুরাগ নদীর ভয়াভহ অবস্থা সম্পর্কে সময় উপযোগী প্রতিবেদন প্রকাশের জন্য The Daily Star পত্রিকা এবং এর রিপোর্টারকে বিশেষ ধন্যবাদ প্রদান করা হলো । নদী রক্ষায় সকল প্রিন্ট এবং ইলেক্ট্রনিক মিডিয়া যে ব্যাপক প্রচারনা এবং সোচ্চার ভূমিকা পালন করে চলেছে তা এক কথায় অতুলনীয়। অত্র রায়ের মাধ্যমে তাঁদের সকলকে অভিনন্দন |

অত্র রায় ও আদেশের অনুলিপি বাংলাদেশের সকল পাবলিক ও প্রাইভেট বিশ্ববিদ্যালয়ের আইন বিভাগের চেয়ারম্যান বরাবরে প্রেরণের জন্য নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো।

অত্র রায় ও আদেশের অনুলিপি অধস্তন আদালতের সকল বিচারককে ইমেইল এর মাধ্যমে পাঠানোর জন্য রে��িষ্ট্রার জেনারেলকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো।

অত্র রায় ও আদেশের অনুলিপি Judicial Administration Training Institute (JATI) তে পাঠানোর জন্য রেজিষ্ট্রার জেনারেলকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো ।

অত্র রায়ের একটি কপি আইন কমিশনের মাননীয় চেয়ারম্যান মহোদয়কে পাঠানোর জন্য রেজিষ্ট্রা জেনারেলকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো।

অত্র রায় ও আদেশের অনুলিপি সকল প্রতিবাদী পক্ষগণকে, শিক্ষামন্ত্রী, প্রধান নির্বাচন কমিশনার, নদী রক্ষা কমিশন, গভর্নর, বাংলাদেশ ব্যাংক, সচিব, শিক্ষা মন্ত্রণালয়, সকল জাতীয় সংসদ সদস্য, সকল উপজেলা চেয়ারম্যান, সকল উপজেলা নির্বাহী প্রয়োজনীয় পদক্ষেপ গ্রহণের নিমিত্তে দ্রুত অবহিত করা হউক । অত্র রায়ের একটি অনুলিপি সরাসরি মাননীয় প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনার বিশেষ মনোযোগ আকর্ষণের নিমিত্ত প্রেরণ করা হোক, যাতে তিনি তাঁর ব্যক্তিগত উদ্যোগে তুরাগ নদীসহ দেশের সকল নদ-নদী রক্ষায় জরুরী ভিত্তিতে পদক্ষেপ নিতে পারেন এবং মাননীয় প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনার নেতৃত্বাধীন সরকার কর্তৃক প্রণীত নদ-নদী রক্ষায় বিশ্বব্যাপী প্রশংসিত আইনসমূহ ভংগকারী দেশ ও মানবতার শক্র অবৈধ নদ-নদী দখলকারী এবং দূষণকারী এবং তাদের সহায়তাকারী সংশ্লিষ্ট সকল সরকারী কর্মকর্তা ও কর্মচারীর বিরুদ্ধে দৃষ্টান্ত সৃষ্টিকারী ব্যবস্থা গ্রহণ করতে পারেন। অত্র রায়ের সহি মহরী অনুলিপি অতি সত্তর বই আকারে বাঁধাই করে রেজিস্ট্রার জেনারেল স্বশরীরে উপস্থিত হয়ে; মাননীয় প্রধানমন্ত্রী সম্মুখে পেশ করবেন। নদীসমূহ বাঁচা মরার উপর বাংলাদেশের অস্তিত্ব জড়িত। অত্র রায়ের যথাযথ বাস্তবায়ন তাই জাতির জন্য খুবই গুরুতৃপূর্ণ। সংশ্লিষ্ট সকল পক্ষ দেশাত্মবোধের চেতনায় উদ্বুদ্ধ হয়ে আন্তরিকতা এবং নিষ্ঠার সাথে দায়িত্ব পালনে সচেষ্ট হলে নিশ্চিতভাবে আমাদের এ দেশটি সুখী, সমৃদ্ধ তথা সর্বকালের সর্বশ্রেষ্ঠ বাঙালী জাতির জনক বঙ্গবন্ধু শেখ মুজিবুর রহমান এঁর স্বপ্নের সোনার বাংলা এবং মাননীয় প্রধানমন্ত্রী শেখ হাসিনার উন্নত বাংলাদেশ হিসেবে গড়ে উঠবে।

পুনশ্চঃ

নদীগুলো চলুক নিরবধি। জোয়ার-ভাটায় নদীগুলো তার ভিন্ন ভিন্ন রূপ দেখতে থাকুক । মাঝি মাল্লারা মনের সুখে আবার নদীতে প্রাণ খুলে ভাটিয়ালী গান গেয়ে উঠুক বাংলার দামাল ছেলেরা নদীতে মনের সুখে আবার দাপাদাপি করুক। মৎস্যজীবীদের মুখের হাসি আবার ফিরে আসুক । পানির ছলাৎ ছলাৎ শব্দে নৌকার মাঝিরা নিশ্চিন্তে ঘুমাক। প্রচুর অর্থের বিনিময়ে দেশ বিদেশে হাওয়াই জাহাজে ঘুরে না বেড়িয়ে বাংলার জনগণ আবার পাল তোলা নৌকায় রূপালী রূপসী বাংলা দেখতে ঘুরে বেড়াক।
