Arguments for the contending parties Nishat-Leave Petitioner

13. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, the learned Advocate for the respondent No. 12, purchaser of Nishat Jute Mills Limited, leave petitioner herein, takes us through the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the documents of purchase of Nishat Jute Mills Limited by the present management i.e. "That's IT Knit Limited" (shortly, IT Knit) from Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation, Government of Bangladesh, connected materials on record and advanced the following arguments before us.

1. Nishat Jute Mills Limited with its properties comprising an area of 22.90 acres of land was purchased by the leave petitioner, purchaser of Nishat. The Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur, upon survey, handed over possession of the same in favour of the present management.

2. From the C.S map, it is clear that the C.S Plots purchased by 'IT Knit' is not within the surrounding area of the river Turag.

3. 'IT Knit' (previous Nishat) is situated on the land purchased from the Government. Therefore, there is no reason to evict the said company from possession of the land which was delivered by the Government.

4. Judicial inquiry report dated 11.10.2017 does not speak that the entire land measuring an area of 22.90 acres is within the land of Turag river. Rather, it is relating to some part of the said land only. The leave petitioner has paid rent to the Government after purchases thereof.

5. There were several joint survey by the Government departments and C.S pillars were also setup by the concerned authority following the direction passed in Writ Petition No. 3503 of 2009. Thus, there was/is no scope to make fresh judicial inquiry/investigation upon survey of the land-in question and directing the leave petitioner and others for their eviction following the judicial inquiry/investigation report.

6. It is true that the jetty of purchaser of Nishat is within the boundary of river Turag but it is being used by Nishat for a long time. Therefore, it cannot be removed from the river as per direction of the Court.

7. The judicial inquiry report is erroneous, imaginary and it was not conducted in their presence and, as such, acceptance of the said report by the High Court Division and passing judgment on the basis of the said report is unlawful and liable to be set aside.

8. While passing the judgment and order, the High Court Division without any reason whatsoever made some extraneous remarks and included some papers having no nexus in deciding the merit of the rule and those ought to be expunged/ deleted from the impugned judgment.

9. The writ-petitioner has not prayed for any declaration that the lease deed executed between the Government and the leave petitioner dated 27.10.2003 is void, unlawful, etc., but the High Court Division travelled beyond the scope of the rule and declared the entire lease document of leave petitioner void, unlawful, etc. although the survey report does not show that 22.90 acres of land owned by the leave petitioner are within the boundary/territory of river Turag.

10. In the above facts and circumstances, the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is erroneous and liable to be set aside.

16. Deliberation of Court

17. It is admitted that previously writ-petitioner HRPB filed another writ petition being Writ Petition No. 3503 of 2009 as a Public Interest Litigation and that as per direction in the said writ petition, the concerned authorities evicted some persons from their unlawful encroachment of river Turag and some other rivers (Buriganga, Balu, Shitalakshya) by demarcating the rivers. However, according to HRPB some persons filed complaints against demarcation of Turag river by evicting some persons but allowing some big and influential encroacher companies and others although those companies and others were also river grabbers. The concerned authority in collusion with those big companies and some private persons allowed those companies/persons to continue their illegal occupation within the boundaries of river Turag including its foreshore. Moreover, there was a rep6rt in "The Daily Star" about encroachment of the river at certain places. In such compelling situation, HRPB had to file Writ Petition No. 13989 of 2016 once again for eviction of all unauthorized persons. In the aforesaid scenario, it cannot be said that the instant writ petition was not maintainable, inasmuch as, due to collusive and unfair demarcation of Turag by the concerned authorities, the writ-petitioner filed the instant writ petition for proper demarcation of the river boundary and eviction of the unauthorized occupant therefrom.

18. "The Daily Star" report dated 06.11.2016 under the heading "Time to declare Turag dead: River grabbers appear mightier than Government, Judiciary; all steps go in vain." along with several photographs attached to this report, clearly gives a picture of the illegal encroachment scenario of Turag in the years 2013, 2014, 2015 and onwards by filling earth, etc. by the land/river grabbers. This detailed report also contains the places of encroachments of Turag river by the river/land grabbers. This report in fact prompted HRPB to file another writ petition and Rule was issued by the High Court Division.

এ স্থানে নদীর সি.এস লাইন হতে নদী অভ্যন্তরে ৪০ফুট পর্যন্ত অবৈধভাবে আর.সি.সি. সীমানা পিলার এবং গাজীপুর সিটি কর্পোরেশন কর্তৃক মাটি দ্বারা ভরাট করে রাস্তা নির্মাণ করা হয়েছে । এ ছাড়াও নদীর সি.এস. লাইন হতে তীর ভূমির পূর্বোক্ত ৫৫ ফুটের মধ্যেও অবৈধ দখলদারগণ কর্তৃক মাটি দ্বারা ভরাট করে সীমানা প্রাচীর নির্মাণ করা হয়েছে। অর্থাৎ এ স্থানে বর্তমানে তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমা হতে তীর ভূমি ও নদীসহ মোট ৯৫ ফুট অবৈধ দখলে আছে। যাতে ভরাটকৃত উচু ভূমি, সীমানা প্রাচীর এবং গাজীপুর সিটি কর্পোরেশন কর্তৃক অবৈধভাবে নির্মিত রাস্তা রয়েছে।

পূর্বানুচ্ছেদে বর্ণিত অনুমিত ৮৮ সংখ্যায়ত পিলার হতে ১৪৫ ফুট দক্ষিণ-পূর্ব দিকে জেরিনা টেক্সটাইল এর দক্ষিণ দিকের সীমানা ও হামীম গ্রুপের মালিকানাধীন সাজিদ ওয়াশিং এর উত্তর দিকের সীমানা প্রাচীর এর মধ্যবর্তী একটি স্থানকে পরিমাপের সুবিধার্থে নদীর Low water Mark এর সীমা হিসেবে চিহ্নিত করা হলো । এ পয়েন্টটির জি.পি.এস, রিডিং Northing ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ১৯.৪” । উল্লেখ্য, এখানে কোন গণপূর্ত বিভাগ স্থাপিত কোন পিলার পরিলক্ষিত হয় নি।

এ স্থানে তীর ভূমির সীমা নদীর উক্ত Low water mark এর  সীমা হতে পূর্ব দিকে (উপরের দিকে) ৬০ ফুট পর্যন্ত বিস্তৃত। তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমার জি-পি.এস, রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪২.০” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২০.০” ।

এ স্থানে বর্ণিত ৬০ ফুট বিস্তৃত তীর ভূমি জেরিনা  টেক্সটাইল অবৈধভাবে ভরাট করেছে। এখানে জেরিনা টেক্সটাইল কর্তৃপক্ষ ২টি বিল্ডিং এর আংশিক অবৈধভাবে তীর ভূমিতে নির্মাণ করেছে।

পূর্বানুচ্ছেদে বর্নিত জেরিনা ফ্যাশন এবং সাজিদ ওয়াশিং এর মধ্যবর্তী স্থানে পরিমাপের সুবিধার্থে গৃহীত কোণ (উপরে বর্ণিত Low water mark যার জি.পি.এস. রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪১.৯” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ১৯.৪” হতে দক্ষিণ পূর্ব দিকে ১৩৬ ফুট এ ১টি পিলার অবস্থিত। এ পিলারটি গণপূর্ত বিভাগ কিংবা BIWTA কর্তৃক স্থাপিত নয়। এ পিলারটির জি.পি.এস. রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪০.৯” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২০.৩”। এ পিলারটি নদীর সি.এস লাইনে অবস্থিত।

এ স্থানে তীর ভূমির সীমা নদীর উক্ত সি.এস. পয়েন্ট হতে (পিলারটি হতে) পূর্ব দিকে উপরের দিকে) ১৫০ ফুট পর্যন্ত বিস্তৃত। তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমার জি.পি.এস, রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪১.৩” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২১.৯” । এখানে তীর ভূমির ক্ষেত্র নিরুপনের সুবিধার্থে ৬৫ নং অনুচ্ছেদে বর্ণিত তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমা হতে (জি.পি.এস. রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪২.০” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২০.০” হতে)।আরো ১০০ ফুট পূর্ব দিকে ১টি পয়েন্ট নির্ধারিত করা হলো। এই পয়েন্টটির জি.পি.এস রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪২.৫” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২১.০”। পূর্বে গৃহীত জি.পি.এস কোওর্ডিনেট Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪২.৫” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২১.০” হতে জি.পি.এস কোওর্ডিনেট Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪১.৩” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২১.৯” পর্যন্ত বিস্তৃত তীর ভূমিতে অবৈধভাবে হা-মীম গ্রুপের ওয়াশিং একাধিক বৃহদাকার কারখানা ভবন নির্মাণ করেছে।

পূর্বানুচ্ছেদে বর্ণিত পিলার (জি. পি. এস কোওর্ডিনেট Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪০.৯” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২০.৩”) হতে ১৬২ ফুট দক্ষিণ দিকে সাজিদ ওয়াশিং ফ্যাক্টরী দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিম কোণের সীমানা ওয়ালের আর.সি.সি. পিলারটি নদীর সি.এস লাইন বরাবর স্থাপিত । এই স্থানের জি.পি.এস রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৩৯.৪” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২১.২”। এ স্থানে তীর ভূমির সীমা নদীর সি.এস. লাইন হতে অর্থাৎ আর.সি.সি পিলারটি (জি.পি.এস রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৩৯.৪” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩’ ২১.২”) হতে পূর্ব দিকে (উপরের দিকে) ১৩৫ ফুট পর্যন্ত বিস্তৃত । তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমার জি.পি.এস রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪০.০” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২২.৮”।

এ স্থানে বর্ণিত তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমা হতে ১৭০ ফুট উত্তরের স্থানে জি.পি.এস রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৪১.৩” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২১.৯” । নদীর তীর ভূমির এ বিস্তৃত এবং ব্যাপক জায়গা অবৈধভাবে দখল করে হা-মীম গ্রুপের মালিকানাধীন সাজিদ ওয়াশিং ফ্যাক্টরী বিশালাকার একাধিক পাকা কারখানা ভবন নির্মাণ করেছে।

উল্লেখ্য যে, আনন্দ গ্রুপের মালিকানাধীন জেরিনা টেক্সটাইল সি.এস ৮১, ৮২, ৮৩ ও ৮৪ নং দাগে এবং হা-মীম গ্রুপের মালিকানাধীন সাজিদ ওয়াশিং ফ্যাক্টরী সি.এস ৮৪, ৮৫, ৮৬ ও ৮৭ নং দাগে অবস্থিত।

(ক) হা-মীম গ্রুপের মালিকানাধীন সাজিদ ওয়াশিং ফ্যাক্টরীর দক্ষিণ পাশের সীমানা প্রাচীরের সর্ব দক্ষিণ-পশ্চিম কোণের আর.সি.সি. পিলারটি নদীর সি.এস. লাইনে অবস্থিত। এ পিলারটির জি.পি.এস রিডিং পূর্বেই বর্ণিত হয়েছে, যা Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৩৯.৪” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২১.২” । এই পয়েন্ট হতে ১০০ ফুট পূর্ব দিকে একটি পিলার বিদ্যমান। এ পিলারটি আনন্দ গ্রুপের গোডাউন এর সীমানা প্রাচীরের উত্তর-পশ্চিম কোনায় অবস্থিত। এটির জি.পি.এস রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩ ৩৯.৬” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২২.৮”।

এ স্থানে তীর ভূমির সীমা নদীর সি.এস. লাইনের উক্ত পিলারটি হতে পূর্ব দিকে (উপরের দিকে) ৩৫ ফুট পর্যন্ত বিস্তৃত।

(খ) পূর্বানুচ্ছেদে বর্ণিত পিলার হতে ১০০ ফুট দক্ষিন দিকে ৯২ সংখ্যায়িত একটি পিলার অবস্থিত। এ পিলারটির জি.পি.এস রিডিং Northing ২৩ ডিগ্রি ৫৩’ ৩৮.৭” এবং Easting ৯০ ডিগ্রি ২৩ ২২.৩”।

এ পিলারটি নদীর সি.এস লাইন হতে ৮৮ ফুট উপরের দিকে অর্থাৎ পূর্ব দিকে স্থাপিত ।

এ স্থানে তীর ভূমির সীমা নদীর সি.এস লাইন হতে পূর্ব দিকে (উপরের দিকে) ১৫৫ ফুট পর্যন্ত বিস্তৃত । অর্থাৎ পিলারটি তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমায় স্থাপন না করে তীর ভূমির শেষ সীমা হতে তীর ভূমির ৬৭ ফুট অভ্যন্তরে স্থাপন করা হয়েছে।”

24. Thus, it appears that Shajid Washing Factory owned by Ha-Meem Groups, Zerina Textile Mills and others encroached upon the river and its fore-shore by constructing factories, etc. within Turag territory.

25. Mr. Mahmud, the learned Advocate for the leave etitioner, failed to show us that the judicial inquiry report is not correct. There were serious allegations that some authorities collusively did not demarcate river Turag as per direction of the High Court Division in the previous writ petition. Therefore, further inquiry/survey by independent person was necessary to ascertain if the concerned authorities in collusion with some big companies and individual did not demarcate Turag river boundary correctly and did not evict them from their illegal occupation within the boundary of Turag. It was also necessary to ascertain river encroachment by differ-ent river grabbers.

26. The leave petitioner claims-that it is the owner of some land by purchase from the Government through an agreement dated 27.10.2003.

27. From this document, it appears that the agreement is between the Government of Bangladesh and "That's It Knit Limited", a private limited company represented by A. K. Azad, Managing Director, who is also representating the leave petitioner. By this agreement, "That's It Knit Limited" purchased some landed properties of Nishat Jute Mills Limited.

28. The schedule of land as described in this agreement is quoted below:

"Summary of Schecule

1. Land (as per Joint Inventory): 22.90 Acres (As per Master Layout) J.L. No. 129, Khatian No. 44/KAT, Dag No. 69 And 107, Mouja, Masimpur, P.S.Tongi, Gazipur

2. Building and other Construction (as per Joint Inventory): a. : Pucca Building 81356 sq.feet b. : Semi Pucca Construction 347470 sq. feet c. : Tin Shed 5834 sq. feet

3. Plant, Machinery and Equpments (as per Joint Inventory)

4. Vehicles: 8 (eight) as per Joint Inventory

5. Furniture and Fixture: as per Inventory"

29. Thus, it appears that by this document, the property of Nishat Jute Mills as described in the schedule was purchased by 'It Knit', a company.

30. According to Mr. Mahmud, the plot numbers as mentioned in this deed are C.S plots. However, in this schedule, it is not mentioned whether the khatian No. 44/KAT, Dag Nos. 69 and 107 of Mouza Masimpur are C.S khatian/plots. Anyway, the other side i.e. HRPB admits it to be C.S plots. From this document, it appears that some land and properties measuring an area of 22.90 acres of C.S. Plot Nos. 69 and 107 were sold by the Government. But on careful scrutiny of the C.S map, it transpires that neither C.S Plot No. 69 nor C.S Plot No. 107 is situated beside the main river Turag.

31. From the argument of Mr. Mahmud, it appears that though C.S Plot Nos. 83 or 81 has not been sold by the Government, but the present management has been using the jetty constructed within the territory of the river in C.S Plot No. 83. There is no scope to construct any jetty within the territory of the river by anyone. Therefore, the leave petitioner not being the owner of this jetty has no legal right to oppose eviction of the unauthorized jetty or eviction some other unlawful structures of Ha-Meem Group and Shajid Washing Factory (Managing Director being A. K. Azad of both) which fall within the boundary of Turag river. It be mentioned that those companies Ha-Meem and Shajid are situated on Plot Nos. 84, 85, 86, 87, etc. beside river Turag by encroaching upon part of river boundary as per judicial inquiry report. We are also of the view that respondent Nos. 10-23 who have encroached Turag river including its fore-shore should remove all earth/sand' filling/ other constructions, etc. from their unlawful encroachment areas of Turag river. If the concerned persons fail to do so, BIWTA and the Deputy Commissioner, Gazipur are to remove such unauthorized occupation by filling earth/sand/other constrctions, etc. following the judicial inquiry report dated 11.10.2017.

32. Mr. Manzill Murshid informed us that all the unauthorized encroachers were evicted from the relevant part of river Turag except respondent Nos. 10-23.

33. Thus, direction No. 6 about removal of the structures, earth/sand fillings, etc. from the river boundary by the High Court Division upon respondent Nos. 10-23 appears to be absolutely lawful and, as such, no interference is necessary.

34. However, it be mentioned that the High Court Division decided ১২নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষকে প্রদত্ত লীজ দলিলের তফসিল সংশ্লিষ্ট জমি পাবলিক ট্রাষ্ট সম্পত্তি তথা জনগণের সম্পত্তি অর্থাৎ রাষ্ট্র উক্ত সম্পত্তির মালিক নন শুধুমাত্র ট্রাষ্টি তথা আমানত গ্রহীতা, সেহেতু সরকার কর্তৃক ১২নং প্রতিবাদী পক্ষকে প্রদত্ত পাবলিক ট্রাষ্ট সম্পত্তির (Public Trust Property)হস্তান্তর দলিল বা লীজ দলিল একটি বেআইনী দলিল। অর্থাৎ দলিলটির সৃষ্টিই হয়েছে পাবলিক ট্রাষ্ট মতবাদের পরিপন্থীভাবে তথা সংবিধান পরিপন্থীভাবে তথা বেআইনীভাবে। সুতরাং একটি ছিল শুরুতেই বাতিল একটি দলিল তথা void ab initio । যে দলিলটি শুরুতেই বাতিল দলিল তার উপর ভিত্তি করে ১২নং প্রতিবাদীপক্ষ কোন প্রতিকার পেতে পারে না।

35. On careful scrutiny of schedule of the agreement of sale of Nishat Jute Mills Limited in favour of the leave petitioner now, in fact, "That's It Knit Limited", as quoted hereinbefore, we do not find that the Government has executed the said agreement including Turag river land. Rather, it is evident that C.S Plot Nos. 81 or/and 83 has/have not been sold to anyone. Therefore, the decision that the document dated 27.10.2003 executed between the Government of Bangladesh and "That's It Knit Limited" is “শুরুতেই বাতিল একটি দলিল তথা void ab initio" is not tenable in law and the said decision is hereby set aside.

36. Now about direction No. 4 of the High Court Division “আগাম প্রতিরোধের নীতি (The Precautionary Principle) এবং দূষনকারী কর্তৃক ক্ষতিপূরণ প্রদানের নীতি (Polluter's Pay Principle) আমাদের দেশের আইনের অংশ হিসেবে ঘোষনা করা হল”. We are of the view that there is no scope for declaring by the Court to treat the Precautionary Principle, Polluter s Pay" Principle" as part of the law of this land as directed by the High Court Division in .its direction No. 4. It is absolutely within the domain of the Parliament.

37. According to our Constitution, the State comprises 3(three) organs-the Legislature, the Judiciary and the Executive. All the or ans have se s arate, well-demarcated functions.

38. It is absolutely within the domain of the Parliament to enact/amend a law fol-lowing the constitutional provisions. However, under article 26 of the Constitution, the State shall not make any law inconsistent with any provision of Part III of the Constitution, and any law so made shall, to the extent of such inconsis-tency, be void.

39. The High Court Division may on an application under article 102 read with article 44 of the Constitution struck down any provision of law made by the Parliament which is violative of fundamental rights of the citizens as provided in part III of the Constitution. Similarly, if the executive/administrative authority of the Government or any statutory body takes any action beyond the law or arbitrarily or malafide, the court may also declare such action illegal and pass necessary directions. The High Court Division may also pass necessary directions to the concerned authorities to protect the biodi-versity, ecological balance and environment, of Bangladesh. But the High Court Division cannot direct the Parliament to enact or amend a law or declare any principle to be a part of our law.

40. However, Mr. Manzill Murshid submits that the above Precautionary Principle and Polluter's Pay Principle have been recognized in our law without specifying such law. If there is such law, the relevant law has to be followed by all concerned and direction No. 4 is redundant.

41. Similarly, we are of the view that the Court may express its opinion only for necessary amendment of a law, for placing the matter to the Parliament as well following necessary procedures by the authority concerned. But it is entirely upon the Parliament to decide as to whether it would amend a law including “জাতীয় নদী রক্ষা কমিশন আইন, ২০১৩” for “নদী দখলকে এবং নদী দূষণকে ফৌজদারী অপরাধ গণ্য করে এর কঠিন সাজা এবং বড় আকারের জরিমানা নির্ধারণ করতঃ. Therefore, direction No. 7 is modified accordingly.

42. Mr. Manzill Murshid failed to show us any law for directing Bangladesh Bank to issue circular, “সেহেতু উক্ত ভূমি দখলের এবং দূষনের অভিযোগ কোন ব্যক্তি বা কোম্পানী বা প্রতিষ্ঠানের বিরুদ্ধে থাকলে উক্ত ব্যক্তি বা কোম্পানী বা প্রতিষ্ঠান সকল প্রকার ব্যাংক ঋণের অযোগ্য মর্মে”. Without backing of any such law, the Court cannot direct for declaring any person ineligible for obtaining bank loan, if there is any allegation of river grabbing or pollution. However, an opinion or suggestion may be given by the court in case of proved encroachment of river to take such measure for public interest. Therefore, direction No. 14 is decided accordingly.

43. Similarly, direction No. 15 upon the Election Commission “সেহেতু উক্ত সম্পত্তি দখলকার এবং দূষণকারী হিসেবে অভিযুক্ত ব্যক্তিকে বাংলাদেশের সকল ইউনিয়ন, উপজেলা, পৌরসভা, জেলা পরিষদ এবং জাতীয় সংসদ নির্বাচনে প্রার্থীর অযোগ্যতা হিসেবে অন্তর্ভূক্ত করে আগামী ৬ মাসের মধ্যে অত্র বিভাগকে হলফনামা সম্পাদনের মাধ্যমে অবহিত করণের জন্য নির্বাচন কমিশনকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হল” cannot be said to be lawful inasmuch as it is the Election Commission to decide the matter in accordance with law. However, the court may give such suggestion/opinion in such matter for public interest.

44. Direction No. 17 is passed by the High Court Division directing- “নদী, প্রকৃতি এবং পরিবেশের উপর নির্মিত দেশ বিদেশের ডকুমেন্টারী ফিল্ম বাংলাদেশ টেলিভিশনে প্রতি শুক্রবার ১ ঘন্টার ১ টি পর্ব সম্প্রচার করার জন্য মহাপরিচালক বাংলাদেশ টেলিভিশন-কে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা গেল। এছাড়া নদী, প্রকৃতি এবং পরিবেশের উপর নির্মিত সপ্তাহে অন্তত ১ দিন ১ ঘন্টার ১ টি ডকুমেন্টারী ফিল্ম প্রচারের জন্য সকল বেসরকারী টিভি চ্যানেলকে নির্দেশ প্রদান করা হলো”. Therefore, the purpose of awareness would be sufficiently served by direction No. 17. Thus, other directions (10, 11, 12, 13 and 16) relating to public awareness are redundant.

<u>45. Before parting with the judgment, we would like to politely point out that the High Court Division, while passing an unnecessary lengthy judgment, has discussed many extraneous matters having no nexus in deciding the merit of the rule. It has also declared a document executed by the Government to be void ab initio without even examining whether by this document the Government has sold any part within the boundary/territory of the river. Moreover, it has also exceeded its jurisdiction relating to some directions as discussed.</u>

46. Further, we would like to note that during pendency of this leave petition, an attempt has been taken by the leave petitioner to change the schedule land/schedule property, as described in its document of purchase dated 27.10.2003. The Government must be very cautious about deciding the matter and the Government shall not under any circumstances lease or sale any land within the boundary of river Turag including foreshore areas, or for that matter, any other river of Bangladesh to protect the biodiversity, ecological balance and environment of Bangladesh.

<u>47. The Government/concerned authorities must bear in mind that at the time of survey, it shall always start the survey from C.S map and then go to RS map and not the other way round.</u>

<u>48. Since, we have heard both the parties at length, we do not think it necessary to grant any leave in this matter which would unnecessarily delay the matter further and thereby allow the unauthorized land/river grabbers to continue with their unlawful possession, further encroachment of the river and thus, destroy the environment of our beloved country, Bangladesh.</u>

49. In view of the above, the rule is disposed of with the observations and directions made in the body of the judgment.

End.

caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.804 of 2018
lawyer:
Mr SK Md. Morshed, Advocate instructed by Ms. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ---- For the Petitioner

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated the 23rd day of February, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.12692 of 2016)
full_judgment:
Abu Bakar Siddiquee J. This civil petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated the 23rd day of February, 2017 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.12692 of 2016 discharging the Rule Nisi.

<u>2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the plaintiff, Girin Ghosh (now deceased), predecessor of the present respondents, filed Land Survey Tribunal Case No.1268 of 2010 for correction of the record of rights of land measuring 8.50 decimals under Dhaka City Survey Khatian No.693, Plot No.9308 on 05.05.20 0, stating, inter alia, that land measuring 2.08 acres appertaining to CS Plot No. 177, Mouza No.297 Begunbari, Police Station-Tejgaon, presently Tejgaon Industrial Area, Dhaka originally belonged to Brojonath Dhupi. which later devolved on his son, Sharat Chandra Dhupi who transferred 1.25 acres land out of 2.08 acres land to Madlona Di Rozario vide registered deed dated 12.06.1950 and after the death of Madloan Di Roziario, her heirs inherited the said land. Subsequently, one Shakhawat Hossain purchased 8.50 decimals land from the heirs of Madlona Di Rozario on 03.12.1988 and accordingly, the land was mutated in his name in 1990. On 25.03.1999, the said land was sold out to the plaintiff, Girin Ghosh and accordingly, the mutation khatian was prepared in his name. The plaintiff established a motor car show room thereon and also by mortgaging the same obtained loan from Janata Bank Limited. Earlier the Government acquired the said land from Madlona Di Rozario on 03.03.1957 and subsequently, derequisitioned the said land in favour of Madlona Di Rozario on 09.07.1962. Thus, the land was enlisted as vested property and at the instance of Madlona Di Rozario, the Government by notice dated 17.12.1989 informed that the land was released from the list of vested property. At the time of City Survey, the khatian of the land was wrongly prepared in the name of Bangladesh Railway, instead of the name of plaintiff, Girin Ghosh; hence the case.</u>

3. The present petitioner, namely, Wega Fashions Sweaters (Pvt) Limited, being added as defendant No.9 on 02.05.2013 contested the case by filing written statement therein contending, inter alia, that the land in question measuring 1.25 acres was acquired by the Government through LA Case No.16 of 1959-60 along with other lands for the purpose of excavation of earth for Bangladesh Railway and accordingly, the Gazette Notification was published on 28.03.1968. After completion of the excavation work, the Government decided to lease out the land for industrial purpose and the present petitioner filed an application to the Ministry of Housing and Public Works for getting the allotment of land and the Ministry vide Memo No.6/1 L-3/95/62 dated 20.10.1996 allotted the said land to the petitioner. Subsequently, the Ministry of Housing and Public Works vide Memo No.Sha-7/L-Tej-18/99/1049/1(2) dated 11.10.2000 directed the concerned Executive Engineer to hand over possession of the said land to the present petitioner as the allottee. Accordingly, the Chief Engineer, Directorate of Public Works vide Memo No.2303/1 dated 12.10.2000 handed over the physical possession of the said land to the petitioner and upon accepting the consideration money, the Government executed the lease agreement on 01.11.2000 and the same was registered in favour of the petitioner. Plaintiff, Girin Ghosh (now deceased), filed Writ Petition No.8741 of 2013 challenging the order dated 02.05.2013 passed in Land Survey Tribunal Case No.1268 of 2010 allowing the application for addition of party of the present petitioner and a Rule was issued on 08.10.2013 and also an order of stay of the operation of order dated 02.05.2013 was passed. But in spite of such stay order, the proceeding of the Land Survey Tribunal case continued. In such facts and circumstances, the petitioner filed an application for stay of the proceeding of the said Land Survey Tribunal Case in Writ Petition No.8741 of 2013 and the said application was allowed by order dated 24.06.2015. Subsequently, the Rule Nisi issued in the said writ petition was discharged for non-prosecution on 14.10.2015. In the meantime, the plaintiff, Girin Ghosh, died on 18.09.2014. But without taking any step for substitution of the heirs of Girin Ghosh, his constituted attorney, Kishore Kumar Saha, PW1, proceeded with the said case by suppressing the fact of death of the sole plaintiff. Bipul Kumar Ghosh, son of the deceased-plaintiff. Girin Ghosh, was substituted on 12.10.2015 as the heir of the deceased-plaintiff in Writ Petition No.8741 of 2013. In the meantime, another writ petition being Writ Petition No.1600 of 2016 was filed by one Akanda Sanowar Murshed and another challenging the order dated 18.10.2012 passed in the said case against the rejection of their application for addition of party and by order dated 22.02.2016, a Rule Nisi was issued and an order of stay of all further proceedings of Land Survey Tribunal Case No.1268 of 2010 was passed. Subsequently, the Rule Nisi in subsequent Writ Petition No.1600 of 2016 was discharged for non-prosecution on 03.08.2016. After disposal of Writ Petition Nos.8741 of 2013 and 1600 of 2016, the proceeding of land survey tribunal case was started. Thereafter, the petitioner filed an application on 25.07.2016 under Order XXII, rule 8 of the Code of Civil Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the Code) for recording an order that the suit has been abated stating, inter alia, that after completion of the deposition of the parties, the case was posted for argument on 15.03.2016. But the heirs of the sole plaintiff were not substituted within the statutory period of 90 days. Then, Bipul Kumar Ghosh, son of late Girin Ghosh, tiled an application on 17.08.2016 for sub-stitution as the heir of sole plaintiff in the said case and both the aforesaid applications for recording the order of abatement of the case and the application for substitution were heard together and the Land Survey Tribunal by order No.47 dated 04.10.2016 allowed the application for substitution and rejected the application for abatement of the case and fixed the matter for argument.

4. Being, aggrieved by order No.47 dated 04.10.2016, the petitioner filed the instant writ petition and obtained the Rule Nisi and the order of stay.

5. Plaintiff-respondent No.8 contested the Rule Nisi by filing an affidavit-in-opposition, denying the material allegations made in the writ petition contending, inter alia, that after disposal of Writ Petition Nos.8741 of 2013 and 1600 of 2016, the petitioner filed an application on 25.07.2016 under Order XXII, rule 8 of the Code for abatement of the case, the deposition of the parties were completed by this time and the case was posted on 15.03.2016 for argument inasmuch as the heir of the sole plaintiff, Girin Ghosh, was substituted in Writ Petition No.8741 of 2013 and as such, the question of abatement of the case does not arise. So, they neither suppressed the facts of death of the plaintiff nor practised fraud upon the Court. The petitioner examined its witnesses as DWs1 and 2 on 17.01.2016 and 08.03.2016 respectively. Bipul Kumar Ghosh, son of late Girin Ghosh, was substituted on 12.10.2015 in Writ Petition No.8741 of 2013, but before that time, the proceeding of the said case was stayed by an order in the same writ petition. Thereafter, the petitioner examined one witness as DW2 and after completion of the deposition when the case was fixed for argument on 15.03.2016, the petitioner filed the said application under Order XXII, rule 8 of the Code with an intention to delay the disposal of the case and as such, the impugned order being rightly passed, 0 e Rule Nisi is liable to be discharged.

6. On perusal of the writ petition, the affidavit-in-opposition as well as annexures thereto and considering the submissions of the learned Advocates for the both sides, the High Court Division discharged the Rule Nisi and vacated the order of stay by the impugned judgment and order dated 23.02.2017. Being aggrieved by and dis-satisfied with the said judgment and order, the petitioner filed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal before this Division.

7. Mr. SK. Md. Morshed, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioner, submits that after completion of the proceedings of Writ Petition Nos.8741 of 2013 and 1600 of 2016, the petitioner filed an application for abatement in Land Survey Case No.1268 of 2010 and along with an application for taking necessary steps against the constituted attorney of Girin Ghosh. Thereafter, present-respondent No.1, Bipul Kumar Ghosh, filed application for substitution in the case on 17.08.2016. He further submits that the case abated automatically under Order XXII, rule 3(2) of the Code in absence of substitution of the legal heirs within the statutory period of 90(ninety) days, but the Tribunal without considering this aspect allowed the substitution petition without any prayer by a separate application for setting aside abatement under Order XXII, rules (2) and (3) of the Code though the same is mandatory requirement of law and as such, the impugned order passed by the Land Survey Tribunal and the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division are liable to be set aside. He further submits that in case of abatement, a formal order of the Court is required for setting aside the said abatement as per Order XXII, rule 9(2) of the Code, but the Tribunal without setting aside the abatement of the said suit allowed the application for substitution of the legal heir of the plaintiff in violation of the provisions of Order XXII, rules 9(2) and (3) of the Code and as such, the impugned order passed by the Tribunal and the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division are liable to be set aside. He further submits that writ-respondent No.8 in his application for substitution filed in Land Survey Tribunal Case No.1268 of 2010 neither made any prayer for setting aside the abatement nor made any explanation for delay in filing the said application and therefore, the impugned order passed by the Tribunal and the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division are liable to be aside. He further submits that the learned Judge in allowing the application for substitution wrongly held that “বাদীপরে দাবী হল মহামান্য হাইকোর্ট বিভাগে রীট পিটিশনের আদেশ এর প্রেক্ষিতে অত্র মোকদ্দমার যাবতীয় কার্যক্রম বন্ধ থাকার কারণে গিরিণ ঘোষের পুত্রকে স্থলাভিষিক্ত করা হয় নি” though there was no order of stay regarding further proceeding of the said case from 18.09.2014 to 24.06.2015 in Writ Petition No.8741 of 2013 and as such, the impugned order passed by the Tribunal is liable to be set aside. He further submits that the application for abatement of the case was filed by the present petitioner on 25.07.2016 and on the other hand, the application for substitution of the sole plaintiff was filed on 17.08.2016, but the learned Judge of the Tribunal failed to take into consideration the mischievous conduct and approach of writ-respondent No.8 before the Court and as such, the impugned order passed by the Land Survey Tribunal is liable to be set aside. He further submits that all the disputes raised by present respondent No.1, Bipul Kumar Ghosh, and his predecessor with regard to the property in question has been resolved in Civil Appeal Nos.62-64 of 2004 and Civil Review Petition Nos.77- 78 and 84 of 2006 and lastly in First Appeal No.371 of 2011. Therefore, continuation of Land Survey Tribunal Case No.1268 of 2010 tiled by Girin Ghosh, father of present respondent No.1, Bipul Kumar Ghosh, regarding correction of the record of right in relation to the said property has become fruitless litigation.

8. Mr. Sasthi Sarker, learned Advocate, appearing for respondent No.1, in his submissions, supported the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division.

9. We have heard the learned Advocate for both the parties and perused the materials on record.

10. An application or substitution of legal heirs of deceased party to a proceeding filed after a period of limitation without making a prayer for setting aside the abatement is to be treated as an application for substitution of the heirs of the deceased party concerned on setting aside abatement. Suffice it to refer the case of Md. Matiur Rahman-Vs-Lal Banu Bibi reported in 1986 BLD 432 wherein it has been held that an application for substitution filed beyond the period of limitation without seeking for an order of setting aside the abatement shall be treated as an application for setting aside the abatement for substitution of the legal heirs. In that view of the matter, our unhesitating conclusion is that the application dated 17.08.2016 can be treated as an application for substitution of the legal heirs of deceased, Girin Ghosh on setting aside abatement.

<u>11. It appears from the application for substitution that the explanation of delay has been furnished but no prayer for setting aside the abatement has been made. The Tribunal allowed such application treating the same as an application for substitution upon setting aside the abatement and on the other hand, it rejected the petitioner's application for recording the order of abatement. The learned Judges of the High Court Division having considered the aforementioned enunciation endorsed the same view upon holding that the Tribunal rightly exercised its discretionary power. The impugned judgment also shows that the learned Judges also disapproved the decision enunciated in the case of Bhupati Biswas-Vs-Niranjon Biswas reported in 40 DLR 517 where no explanation of delay was furnished. We are inclined to hold that the Courts below rightly exercised its discretionary power upon proper appreciation of fact, the superior Court shall not interfere therewith.</u>

12. It may be mentioned further that the heirs of Girin Ghosh have been substituted in Writ Petition Nos.8741 of 2013 and 1600 of 2016, where the legal representatives of a party to a proceeding have already been brought on record which is connected and inter dependent proceeding even though in superior Court, side by side the preceding of the case before the Tribunal was stayed in the aforesaid writ petition. Thus, it is totally unnecessary to insist upon a repetition of the same process in the lower Court and in such a case, the question of abatement does not arise.

13. Having considered those facts and circumstances, evidence on record, we find no illegality and infirmity in the impugned judgment.

14. Therefore, we find no reason to interfere with the decision and findings of the High Court Division.

15. Accordingly, we find no merit in this civil petition for leave to appeal and the same is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

case_source: (From the judgment and order dated 01.09.2016 passed by the Appellate Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1690 of 2014.)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique J. Delay is condoned.

2. This civil review petition is directed against the judgment and order dated 01.09.2016 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1690 of 2014.

3. The respondent, while serving as an Additional District Judge, was dismissed from service by an order dated 23.08.2004. He filed a review petition before the Hon'ble President of the Republic against the said order of dismissal which was rejected on 07.02.2011. Thereafter, he filed Administrative Tribunal Case No.50 of 2011 before the Administrative Tribunal, Bogra which was allowed on 20.02.2012. Appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal preferred by the Government was dismissed on 11.04.2012 as being time barred. The Government then filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.1690 of 2014 in this Division which was also dismissed as being time barred. Then the Government has filed this review petition.

4. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Attorney General appearing for the review petitioner, at the outset, drawing our attention to the date of the order of dismissal and date of filing the case before the Administrative Tribunal, submits that the instant Administrative Tribunal case was hopelessly barred by limitation which was not properly addressed in the Administrative Tribunal, thereby, it erroneously entertained the Administrative Tribunal Case. He submits that it is a fit case to exercise jurisdiction of this Division vested under article 104 of the Constitution otherwise an act without jurisdiction would get seal of validation. He further submits that the Inquiry Officer, finding the charge Nos.3, 4 and 5 brought against the delinquent officer proved, submitted his report and the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs, taking the approval of the Supreme Court, dismissed him from the service. He submits that Full Court of the Supreme Court approved the proposal of dismissal of the delinquent officer and the learned Chief Justice of Bangladesh presided over the meeting of the Full Court, in which, Supreme Court approved the decision of dismissal, the Administrative Tribunal ignored decision of the Full Court of the Supreme Court although there was no finding about any malafide or the decision taken by the Full Court was corum non-judice.

5. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud, learned Senior Counsel appearing for the respondent, submits that the appeal before the Administrative Appellate Tribunal was time barred and it, finding the appeal as being time barred, dismissed the same. He submits that limitation to prefer appeal is a special limitation provided in the Administrative Tribunal Act, the Administrative Appellate Tribunal did not commit any error of law in dismissing the appeal. He further submits that the Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal as well as review petition were also time barred, in such view of the matter, the review petition should be dismissed.

6. It appears from the materials on record that the respondent was dismissed from service on 23.08.2004. He filed review petition before the Hon'ble President of the Republic on 25.04.2004 which was rejected on 07.02.2011 and the petitioner filed the instant Administrative Tribunal Case before the Administrative Tribunal on 28.04.2011, that is, about 7 years after passing the order of dismissal.

<u>7. To examine the point of limitation, decision of this Division in the case of Md. Sirajul Islam Khan Vs. Bangladesh Bank, Dhaka and others reported in XIII ADC 289 is relevant here. In the cited case, 8(eight) members bench of this Division has observed,</u>

<u>"It appears that a new second proviso has been inserted after proviso No. 1 in Sub-Section (2) of Section 4 by the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act 1997 (Act No.24 of 1997). According to the said amended provision of Section 4(2) of the Administrative Tribunals Act the appeal pending before the Higher Administrative Authority shall be deemed to have been disallowed by the authority after the expiry of two months from the date of submissions of the departmental appeal and accordingly the appellant ought to have filed the A.T. Case within six months after the expiry of said two months before the Administrative Tribunal but he did not do so and as such the case before the Administrative Tribunal was barred by limitation. In Civil Petition for leave to appeal No.1454 of 2008, Bangladesh Supreme Court Digest -2009, Volume-XII, Page.10 the fact was that the petitioner was dismissed from service on 24.01.1995. He preferred departmental appeal on 08.02.1995 and it was rejected on 14.01.2001. In the meantime the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1997 (Act No. XXIV of 1997) came into force on 19.11.1997 whereby new 2nd proviso to section 4(2) of the Act was introduced. This Division approved the view taken by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal that as the amending Act came into force on 19.11.1997 the appeal to the higher authority by the petitioner deemed to have been rejected on 19.01.1998 i.e. before 19.07.1998 but he filed the A.T. Case on 4.06.2001 long after the statutory period of limitation. Therefore, the Administrative Tribunal Case was hopelessly barred by limitation under section 4(2) of the A.T. Act, 1980. In Abul Bashar Vs. Investment Corporation of Bangladesh and another, 20 BLD(AD)294 the fact was that the petitioner was an Assistant General Manager of the Investment Corporation of Bangladesh. In exercise of powers under Regulation 56(2) the Investment Corporation of Bangladesh (Officers and Employees) Service Regulations, 1993 the Investment Corporation of Bangladesh terminated the service of the petitioner, as Assistant General Manager of the Corporation on 23 April 1995. The petitioner challenged the order of termination in Writ Petition No.921 of 1995. The petition was summarily rejected on 3 May 1995. The petitioner, thereafter, made a civil petition for leave to Appeal before the Appellate Division which was also summarily rejected on 13 December 1995. Being unsuccessful, the petitioner filed case No.242 of 1995 before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka, on 31 December 1995. being unsuccessful, the petitioner filed case No.242 of 1995 before the Administrative Tribunal, Dhaka, on 31 December 1995,which was beyond time. He, however, sought to have the benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act on the ground that the time spent for prosecution of the writ petition and the civil petition for leave to appeal should be excluded in computation of the period of limitation prescribed under the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980. This Division held that it is clear from the wording of the second proviso (Now that is third after the amendment of 1997) to subsection (2) of section 4 of the Administrative Tribunals Act that the legislative intendment behind this provision is to exclude the proceedings governed by the Administrative Tribunals Act from the operation of the benefit conferred by sub-section(2) of section 29 of the Limitation Act, 1908 and while computing the period of limitation in filing an application before the Administrative Tribunal a person can not have the benefit of section 14 of the Limitation Act, 1908. This judgment justifies that limitation in regard to cases under Administrative Tribunals Act, 1980 has to be calculated applying the procedures described in the Act itself and there is very little scope, if not no scope. To deviate from the strict rule of limitation embodied in the Act while dealing with Administrative Tribunals cases.</u>

<u>From the above discussions and findings we are of the view that both the Tribunals below having considered the materials on record rightly arrived at a correct decision in the matter. Accordingly, we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order passed by the Administrative Appellate Tribunal in affirming those passed by the Administrative Tribunals."</u>

8. In view of the decision referred above, it is apparent on the face of the record that the instant Administrative Case was hopelessly barred by limitation since the respondent filed the instant case before the Administrative Tribunal after about 7 years of arising its cause of action inasmuch as he was entitled to get 2 months+6 months time to file A.T. Case in view of the second proviso as added in Section 4 of the Administrative Tribunal Act by the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1997 and the interpretation of this Division quoted above. The Administrative Tribunal relied upon the case of Jahangir Kabir (Md.) V. Bangladesh reported in 48 DLR (AD) 156 but the said A.T. case was instituted in 1987 and Appeal was preferred in 1991 and C.A. was preferred and disposed of in 1995, that is, the same was decided by this Division before amendment of Section 4(2) of the Act by Act XXIV of 1997. This A.T. Case has been filed in 2011, that is, long after the said amendment. The Administrate Tribunal, ignoring the aforesaid facts, most unfortunately, entertained the A.T. case referring Jahangir Kabir's case.

<u>9. The learned Attorney General submits that the Administrative Tribunal had no jurisdiction to entertain the instant case since the same was hopelessly barred by limitation and that Tribunal was not authorized to con-done the delay. The jurisdiction means the authority by which the a Court/tribunal has to decide the matter that litigated before it, or to take cognizance of matters presented in a formal way for its decision. It is the authority to hear and determine cause, to adjudicate and exercise any judicial power in relation to it. The jurisdiction of the Court/ Tribunal may be qualified as restricted by variety of circumstances. The power of the tribunal may be exercised within the limitation provided by the statute. Such limitation of exercising power has been imposed by the Administrative Tribunal Act itself. The essence of the matter was whether the tribunal had power to entertain time barred case and to grant relief. Since the Tribunal was not authorised to entertain time barred case, the decision given by the tribunal was a nullity. The Administrative Tribunal cannot ignore the law declared by the highest Court of the Country and initiate proceeding ignoring the law so declared. The Administrative Tribunal also ignored the decision of 5 members Bench of this Division, that is, case of Abul Basher Vs. Investment Corporation of Bangladesh reported in 20 BLD(AD)294 as quoted earlier.</u>

10. The Administrative Appellate Tribunal had no opportunity to entertain the time barred appeal in view of the Special Limitation provided in the Act to prefer appeal. In view of peculiar circumstances, question arises as to whether this Court would shut its eyes or not.

11. In the case of National Board of Revenue Vs. Nasrin Banu reported in 48DLR(AD)171 this Division observed that the words 'complete justice' do not yield to a precise definition. Cases vary, situations vary and the scale and parameter of complete justice also vary. Sometimes it may be justice according to law, sometimes it may be justice according to fairness, equity and good conscience, sometimes it may be in the nature of arbitration, sometimes it may be justice tempered with mercy, sometimes it may be pure commonsense, sometimes it may be the inference of an ordinary reason-able man and so on. It can invoke such jurisdiction whenever it is of the opinion that such power requires to be activated in a given situation that comes to its notice.

12. The power conferred under Article 104 of the Constitution to this Court is under special circumstances and for special reason having the concept of justice being predominate factor being the inclusion of such an article in the Constitution. Here in this case it appears to us that the Administrative Tribunal has committed a grave and patent error which cannot be otherwise remedied and that the decision of the Tribunal so far the same relates to limitation of filing A.T. case is concerned is based on total misconception and misapplication of the law which touches the exercise of its jurisdiction. In view of such circumstances, this Court may interfere the same in exercise of its extraordinary power.

13. We are of the view that in order to resolve the peculiar circumstances it is a fit case for exercise our power vested under article 104 of the Constitution.

14. In the recent case of Md. Aynul Haque Vs. Government of Bangladesh passed in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.64 of 2010, this Division observed that the facts revealed serious scandal of corruption in connection with his judicial functions. The reputation of being corrupt would gather thick and unchaseable clouds around the conduct of an officer and gain notoriety must faster than the smoke. Sometimes there may not be concrete or material evidence to establish the same beyond all reasonable doubt. Judicial service is not a service in the sense of an employment as is commonly understood. Members of the judicial service, exercising judicial functions, are distinct from the members of other services. Their honesty and integrity is expected to be beyond doubt. It should be reflected in their judicial functions and their over all reputations. There is no manner of doubt that nature of Judicial service is such that it cannot afford to suffer continuance in service of persons of doubtful integrity. Dishonesty is the stark antitheses of judicial polity. We do not make any comment regarding charges as found by the Inquiry Officer proved but to say that the same is unfortunate for the judiciary.

<u>15. In Md. Aynal Haque's Case (supra) we have already given our observation regarding the authority of the Tribunal to examine the decision of the Full Court which runs as follows:</u>

<u>"Submission of Mr. Farooquie that whether the decision of Full Court is amenable or not it is to say that in the very nature of things it would be difficult, nearing almost an impossibility to subject such exercise undertaken by the Full Court except in an extra ordinary case when the Court is convinced that some real injustice, which ought not to have taken place, has really happened and not merely because there could be another possible view or someone has some grievance about the exercise undertaken by the Full Court. If the authority bonafide forms an opinion relying upon some materials that over all integrity of a judicial officer is doubtful, the correctness of such opinion cannot be challenged in the court unless any violation of law or gross injustice is done. Mr. Farooquie failed to show that opinion formed by the Full Court was arbitrary or capricious or said to be irrational so as to shock the conscience of the Court to warrant or justify any interference."</u>

16. Since we are of the view that the Administrative Tribunal case was not maintainable as being hopelessly time barred the question as to whether the charges brought against the respondent have been proved or not does not deserve any consideration. But it is to be narrated clearly that cancerous cells of corruption constantly keep creeping into the vital veins of the judiciary and need to stem it out by judicial surgery for keeping the stream of justice delivery system unpolluted.

17. Considering the facts and circumstances, we are of the view that the Administrative Tribunal cannot pass an ex hypothesi decision and, as such, interference over the matter is called for.

18. Accordingly, the order dated 01.09.2016 passed by this Division is reviewed and set aside. The decisions of the Administrative Tribunal and the Administrative Appellate Tribunal are set aside.

19. Thus, the review petition is disposed of.

End.

7. In writ petition No. 2035 of 2014, the Rule was issued in the following terms: Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed not to demolish the petitioner's No. l's building and boundary walls or any part thereof standing on 0.0325 acres of land situated at Mouza Kafrul, Police Station-Kafrul, JL No. 268, SA 101, RS 11, City Zarip Mouza No. 6, CS and SA Dag No. 315, RS Dag No. 5144, of CS Khatian No. 400 and SA Khatian No. 286 corresponding to Municipal Holding No. 146 which is butted and bounded on the East City Corporation Road, on the West and South Abdul Awal Municipal Holding No. 147, on the North Abdul Hamid, and further to show cause as to why the respondents shall not be directed not to demolish the petitioners No. 2 to 8's building and boundary walls or any part thereof standing on 0.0451 acres of land situated at Mouza-Kafrul, Police Station-Kafrul, CS No. 268, SA 101, RS 11 City Zarip Mouza No. 6, CS and SA Dag No. 315 RS Dag No. 5144 of CS Khatian No. 400 and SA Khatian No. 286 corresponding to Municipal Holding No. 145 which is butted and bounded on the East Abdul Awal, Municipal Holding No. 147 on the West City Corporation Road, on the South City Corporation Road and on the North Soleman Municipal Holding No. 146, and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

8. In writ petition No. 2580 of 2014, the Rule was issued in the following terms: Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why they should not be directed not to demolish the petitioner's house and boundary wall or any part thereof standing on 0.057 acre of land situated at Mouza-Kafrul, Police Station-Kafrul, JL No. 268, CS and SA Dag No. 313(Part) of CS Khatian No. 400 and SA Khatian No. 287 DP Khatian No. 2429, Plot No. 4188 corresponding to Municipal Holding No. 33, which is butted and bounded on the East City Corporation Road, on the West Abdur Rashid, Municipal Holding No. 35, on the South Shafiuddin Ahmed, Municipal Holding No. 34 and on the North Late Syed Ahmed, Municipal Holding No. 32 and/or pass such other or further No. 32 and/or pass such other or further order or orders as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

9. The facts necessary for disposal of the Rules, in brief are that: The petitioners became the owner of the suit land and they are in possession in suit land by way of purchase or inheritance and after mutating their names in City Zarip, constructed building thereon by the authorized plan passed by the Cantonment Board/RAJUK. The petitioners filed writ petitions being No. 861/2004, 865/2004, 863/2004, 859/2004, 866/2004, 864/2004, 867/2004, 871/2004, 868/2004 and 869/2004 before the Hon'ble High Court Division by challenging the notice for re-hearing of the Appeal Cases No. 62573/2002, 63305/2002, 62575/2002, 62577/2002, 62579/2002, 65095/ 2002, 65102/2002, 62584/2002, 62583/2002, 62576/2002 and 65101/2002 by the respondents. 

10. The said writ petitions were heard analogously and those Rules were discharged on 12-6-2012 with observations that the writ petitioners are at liberty to invoke the proper forum as provided under Section 145A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950. As per the said observations, the petitioners (except in writ petition Nos.2581/2014 and 2580/2014) filed Land Survey Suit Nos. 8 of 2013, 15/2013, 14/2013, 10/2013, 11/2013, 13/2013, 16/2013, 18/2013 and before the Land Survey Tribunal Dhaka Mohanagor which is still pending. 

11. Against the said respective judgments and orders (in writ petitions being No. 2581/2014 and 2580 of 2014), the petitioners filed Civil Miscellaneous Case Nos.704/2012 and 702/2012 before the Apex Court and. The Apex Court gave (eight) weeks stay of operation of the judgment and order dated 12-6-2012 and had directed to file regular leave petition.

12. Since the matters are pending before Appellate Division, threaten to demolish the petitioners' structure and residential houses without due process of law is a violation of natural justice. 

13. Finding no other alternative efficacious remedy, the petitioners have moved this Court and obtained the instant Rule Nisi. 

14. The respondent Nos. 5 Sr 9 to 12 respectively filed the affidavits in opposition. 

15. The case of respondent No.5 (in writ petition No. 2037 of 2014), in short is that: The suit land has been acquired vide LA Case No.30/70-71 by the National Housing Authority for constructing road from Mirpur section-01 to Cantonment via Kochukhet. On 13-10-1988, considering public interest the suit land was handed over by the National Housing Authority to the then Dhaka Municipal Corporation now Dhaka North City Corporation for developing and constructing road in the said area. As the suit land was handing over by the National Housing Authority now the owner of the suit land is Dhaka North City Corporation. Thus, the suit land is the property of Dhaka North City Corporation under the government and the petitioner does not have any right title and interest over the suit land. 

16. The cases of the respondent Nos. 9 & 10 respectively is that : 
The Dhaka North City Corporation is a statutory body created under the Local Government (City Corporation) Act, 2009, as amended in 2011. This Act has divided the then Dhaka City Corporation into two separate institutions, namely Dhaka South City Corporation and Dhaka North City Corporation. Within its • territorial jurisdiction, Dhaka North City Corporation is responsible for providing a range of services to citizens with a view to ensuring that citizens enjoy civic amenities. 

17. The Dhaka North City Corporation subsequently took initiative to build road in 2014 before the commencement of the ICC 1-20 World Cup held in Bangladesh and Dhaka North City Corporation handed over responsibility to build the road on the said acquired land to Army Engineering Battalion (14th Independent Engineering Brigade). The said Battalion has already constructed the concerned road up to 60%, but because of the ad-interim restraining order the rest of the work has remained stopped, which is creating serious traffic problem and the said road needs to be completed as soon as public interest, hence the Rules are liable to be discharged. 

18. Mr Taufiq Sajawar Partho, learned Assistant Attorney-General on behalf of the respondent No.5 submits that on 13-10-1988, considering the public interest the suit land was handed over by the National Housing Authority to the then Dhaka Municipal Corporation, now, Dhaka North City Corporation for developing and constructing road in the said area. He next contends that the suit land is under the acquired land and hence the Purchase of acquired land is not valid. 

19. Mr KS Salah Uddin Ahmed, learned Advocate on behalf of the respondent Nos.9 & 10 has adopted the submission of the learned Assistant Attorney-General and in addition, the learned Advocate further submits that the writ petitioners have filed these writ petitions appertaining to those lands which are acquired by the government and the petitioners are trying to grab the said land by constructing illegal structure. He further submits that the Planning Commission had extended the tenure of the project and if the said project is not completed within the stipulated period, the project will be frustrated. He further submits that the writ petitioners are trespassers on the disputed land which has been acquired for construction of a road in the public interest. He lastly contends that the disputed question which the writ petitioners have raised can in no way be determined in a summary jurisdiction like writ jurisdiction, as such, these writ petitions are not maintainable and are liable to be discharged. 

20. Mr Mahbubey Alam, learned Senior Advocate appearing with learned Advocate Mr Md Imam Hasan (in writ petition No. 2581 of 2014) on behalf of the respondent Nos.11-12 submits that neither the petitioner made any statements against the RAJUK in the writ petition nor sought any relief against the RAJUK and RAJUK is no way connected with the subject matter of the instant writ petition and a such Rule is liable to be discharged. 

21. We have perused the writ petitions, its annexures, affidavits in opposition filed by the respective respondents and affidavits in reply filed by the petitioners and other materials on record placed before us. 

22. The moot question to be considered in these Rules is whether acquisition of the land of petitioners has been made for public purpose or not and whether such acquisition has been made following the due procedure. 

23. Annexure-II to the affidavits-in-opposition of the respective writ petitions filed by the respondent Nos. 9 & 10 is the schedule of the land in question which has been published in the Bangladesh Gazette on 20th February, 1980 and the map of the lands in question has already been published. 

24. We note that since the petitioners have changed the nature of the land in question to be their own land, we are of the view whether the land of the petitioners falls within the acquisition is a disputed question of fact and such question cannot be resolved without measurement and taking evidence within is beyond the purview of the writ jurisdiction. Reliance is placed on the decision in Nasirullah and another vs Bangladesh and others, reported in 61 DLR 119. 


25. It transpires further from the record that the land in question had been acquired vide LA case No. 30/70-71 for constructing road from Mirpur section 14 to Cantonment via Kochukhet by the National Housing Authority for the public interest. 

26. It is now well established that Courts can examine the purpose of the acquisition to determine whether or not it has been made for a public purpose. The Privy Council in Hamabi Framjee Petit vs Secretary of State for India in Council, 42 Ind App 44 : (AIR 1914 PC 20), stated the law in these words. 
"Prima facie the Government are good judges of that (public purpose) but they are not absolute judges. They cannot say "sic volo sic jubeo," but at least a Court would not easily hold them to be wrong" 

27. Again; the Supreme court in State of Bombay vs RS Nanji, (S) AIR, 1956 SC 294, laid down : 
"Prima-facie the Government is the best judge as to whether 'public purpose' is served by issuing requisition order, but it is not the sole judge. The Courts have the jurisdiction and it is their duty to determine the matter whenever a question is raised whether a requisition order is or is not for a 'public purpose'." 

28. From these, it follows that it is open to this Court sitting under writ jurisdiction provided under Article 102 of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh to determine whether or not the acquisition in the present cases have been made for a public purpose. The point to be determined in each case relating to the private and public interest has been held in the case of State of Bihar vs Sir Kameshwar Singh, reported in AIR 1952 SC 252 where it was observed that : 
"The concept of public purpose there is a negative element in that no private, interest can be created in the property acquired compusorily; in other words, property of someone cannot be acquired to be given to someone for his own private purposes and that there is a positive element in the concept that the property taken must be for public benefit" 

29. Again, in the same case it was further held that: 
"The sovereign power to acquire property compulsorily is a power to acquire it only for a public purpose. There is no power in the sovereign to acquire private property in order to give it to private persons. Public purpose is a content of the power itself." 
"As between individuals, no necessity, however great, no exigency, however imminent, no improvement, however valuable, no refusal, however un-neighborly, no obstinacy, however unreasonable, no offers of compensation, however extravagant, can compel or require any man to part with an inch of his estate." 

30. The Privy Council in 42-Ind App cases has observed : 
"It is this element of the general interest of the community which transforms the purpose into a public purpose." 

31. Nichols in his well known book "The Law of Eminent Domain" stated that: 
"If the use for which land is taken by eminent domain is public, the taking is not invalid merely because an incidental benefit will inure to private individuals." 

32. When the property is acquired for project to be implemented by the Government, the object/purpose of acquisition is treated as for public. Whereas, when the property is acquired for project to be implemented and funded by body other than Government and the project is for public good or public use, the object/purpose of acquisition is treated as public interest. In the case of Government of Bangladesh vs Md Gias Uddin Chowdhury, 2012 BLD (AD) 1 = 17 BLC (AD) 14, their Lordships observed: 
"As soon as a piece of land is acquired in accordance with law the owner is deprived of his right. A citizen holds his property, subject always to the right of the sovereign to take it for a public purpose. This right is called eminent domain. The right of eminent domain is the right of the sovereign State through its regular agencies." 

33. In the light of the finding made herein-above, this Court of the view that this Court will not interfere with the acquisition since the acquisition was for public purpose and there is nothing which shows that law was violated in the process of acquisition. 

34. In view of the above discussions made hereinbefore, the Rules being devoid of merit are bound to fail. 

35. Accordingly, the Rules are discharged. The interim order of restraint granted at the time of issuance of the Rules are hereby vacated. 

36. There is, however, no order as to costs. 

Communicate the judgment and order at once. 

End.

full_judgment:
Borhanuddin, J: This Income Tax Reference application at the instance of the assessee-applicant Commissioner of Taxes, Taxes Zone-1, Dhaka, arises out of an order dated 30-6-2003 passed by the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Division Bench-3, Dhaka, in Income Tax Appeal No.5189 of 2001-2002. This is relating to the assessment year 1997-98. 

2. Brief facts are that the respondent-assessee submitted Income Tax Return for the assessment year 1997-98 showing total income including income from Capital Gains at Taka 32,89,047 to the Deputy Commissioner of Taxes, Circle-5, Taxes Zone-1, Dhaka (hereinafter called as "the DCT") who completed assessment under Section 83(2) computing total income of the assessee at Taka 1,56,19,453. Being aggrieved, the assessee preferred appeal before the Additional Joint Commissioner of Taxes (hereinafter stated as "the AJCT") Dhaka. Upon hearing the parties, the AJCT deleted income from capital gains and directed the DCT to take steps after knowing locally regarding transfer of flats. In compliance of the appeal order, the DCT revised the assessment under Section 83(2)/156 of the Ordinance. Being dissatisfied, the assessee filed appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Division Bench-4 agitating estimation of annual family expenditure. The appeal was numbered as ITA No. 2954 of 1998-99. The Department also filed appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal against the order of the AJCT agitating the point of deleting income from capital gains. The appeal was numbered as ITA No.4104 of 1998-99. Upon hearing the appeal filed by the assessee, Tribunal reduced the family expenditure from Taka 1,50,000 to Taka 1,27,000 and after hearing the appeal filed by the department, Tribunal upheld the order passed by the AJCT regarding income from capital gains by its order dated 31-12-1998. Accordingly, DCT revised the assessment on 28-1-1999. At this stage, the Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes (hereinafter stated as "the IJCT) suo muto reopened case of the assessee under section 120 of the Ordinance and computed total income of the assessee at Taka 1,42,37,953 taking into consideration income from capital gains. 

3. Being aggrieved by the order of the IJCT, the assessee filed appeal before the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) [hereinafter stated as "the CT(A)"], Taxes Zone-1, Dhaka. After hearing the parties the CT(A) upheld order of the IJCT. Being aggrieved, the assessee filed second appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal which is numbered as ITA No. 5189 of 2001-02. Upon hearing the parties, Tribunal upheld order of the CT(A). Thereafter the assessee filed a Miscellaneous application being No. 25/2003-04 before the Tribunal for rectification error of the order passed in ITA No. 5189/2001-2002. Tribunal after hearing the parties allowed the application vide order dated 26-8-2003. Against the order, the applicant herein filed instant reference application formulating the following questions of law: 
I) Whether the learned Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Division Bench-3, Dhaka was legally justified in reversing its own order passed in ITA No. 5189 of 2001-2002 (Assessment year 1997-98) by admitting a miscellaneous application on it from the assessee applicant and passing the order in MA No. 25 of 2003-2004 by violating the provision of sub-section (5) of section 159 of the IT Ordinance, 1984? 
II) Whether the learned Taxes Appellate Tribunal, Division Bench-3, Dhaka was legally justified in vacating the order of the Commissioner of Taxes (Appeal) and order under section 120 of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984 of the Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes on the ground that the Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes acted beyond his jurisdiction by invoking action under section 120 as the issue is settled in Tribunal whereas the Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes only re-examined whether the assessee has reinvested the Capital Gains under section 32(8) as per direction of the Appellate Joint Commissioner of Taxes which was upheld by the Taxes Appellate Tribunal Division Bench-2, Dhaka ? 

4. The respondent has opposed the reference application by filling affidavit-in-reply denying the averments made in the reference application and supporting the order of the Tribunal. It has been stated that the grounds taken in the reference application are defective, misleading, misconceived and the questions posed are not proper questions of law and so, no answer is required in the reference application and it is liable to be rejected. It is also stated in the affidavit that the IJCT had no jurisdiction to invoke section 120 of the Ordinance after order of the DCT relating to income from capital gains has been merged with the order passed by the Tribunal in 2nd appeal. 

5. Ms. Mahfuza Begum, learned Deputy Attorney-General appearing for the applicant submits that the Tribunal erred in law in entertaining the miscellaneous application filed by the assessee respondent under section 173 of the Ordinance but she failed to answer whether the IJCT had jurisdiction to invoke section 120 of the Ordinance after order of the DCT merged with the order passed in 1st appeal and thereafter in 2nd appeal before the Tribunal. 

6. On the other hand, Mr Md Abu Amzad learned advocate appearing for the respondent assessee submits that when the issue has been settled by the Tribunal in that stage the IJCT had no jurisdiction to invoke section 120 of the Ordinance relating to selfsame matter. 

7. Upon going through the facts and circumstances as well as core issue involve it appears that the applicant has failed to bring out the relevant question. Therefore, we would like to reformulate the same in the following manner: 
(i) Whether on the facts and in the circumstances of the case Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes had authority to invoke section 120 of the Ordinance after the issue was settled vide order of the Appellate Tribunal. 

8. We have examined the reference application and the annexure appended thereto as well as affidavit-in-reply and supplementary affidavit. 

9. It is admitted position that the assessee-applicant submitted his return for the assessment year 1997-98 and the assessment was made by the DCT under section 83(2) of the Ordinance. Being aggrieved by the order of the DCT the assessee preferred two appeals firstly before the AJCT and then before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal No. 4 and the assessee got partial relief from 1st and 2nd appellate authorities. It is to be mentioned here that the department also filed appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal and the Tribunal after hearing affirmed the order passed by the AJCT relating to income from capital gains. Therefore, it is evident that the assessment by the DCT merged with the order of the appellate authority. Under section 120 of the Ordinance Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes may revise assessment order of the DCT under Section 83(2) of the Ordinance if he considers that any order passed by the DCT is erroneous in so far as it is prejudicial to the interest of the revenue. But in the instant case order of the DCT was challenged upto the Tribunal and finally concluded there. Therefore, the order of the DCT merged with the order of the Tribunal. 

10. The doctrine of merger is neither a doctrine of constitutional law nor a doctrine statutorily recognized. It is a common law doctrine founded on principles of propriety in the hierarchy of justice delivery system. It has been decided by the apex courts of this sub-continent. 

11. The logic underlying the doctrine of merger is that there cannot be more than one decree or operative orders governing the same subject-matter at a given point of time. When a decree or order passed by inferior court, tribunal or authority was subjected to a remedy available under the law before a superior forum then, though the decree or order under challenge continues to be effective and binding nevertheless its finality is put in jeopardy. Once the superior court has disposed of the lis before it either way whether the decree or order under appeal is set-aside or modified or simply confirmed, it is the decree or order of the superior court, tribunal or authority which is the final, binding and operative decree or order wherein merges the decree or order passed by the court, tribunal or the authority below. 

12. There can be no doubt that since an appeal is provided against an order passed by the DCT, the decision of the appellate authority is the operative decision in law. If the appellate authority modifies or reverses the decision of the DCT, it is obvious that it is the appellate decision that is effective and can be enforced. In law the position would be just the same even if the appellate decision merely confirms the decision of the DCT. As a result of the confirmation or rebuttal of the decision of the DCT by the appellate authority the original decision merges in the appellate decision and it is the appellate decision alone which subsists and is operative and capable of enforcement. 

13. This view of ours is also supported by the decision in the case of Sonali Agency vs National Board of Revenue, reported in 13 MLR (HCD) 313 = 60 DLR 310 as well as the case of Mohammad Kamrul Ashraf Khan vs Commissioner of Taxes, Taxes Zone-4, Dhaka, reported in করাদালত, মার্চ-২০০৩.

14. In the instant case it is admitted that department filed appeal before the Taxes Appellate Tribunal against order of the AJCT relating to income from capital gains and the Tribunal upheld order of the AJCT and the department did not prefer any reference application against order of the Tribunal. In the circumstances, we find that Inspecting Joint Commissioner of Taxes has got no power to invoke jurisdiction under section 120 of the Ordinance for revision of the assessment as was made by the DCT. Thus, we are of the opinion that the Tribunal was justified in deciding the legal question that the IJCT had no scope to reopen of the case under section 120 of the Ordinance after the assessment was completed finally by the Tribunal. 

15. Thus, we find no merit in the submission of Ms. Mahfuza Begum and we find merit in the submission of Mr Md Abu Amzad. 

16. In the result our answer to the question reformulated is in the negative i.e. in favour of the assessee-respondent. 

17. Accordingly, the reference application is disposed of. 

18. No order as to cost. 

The Registrar of the Bangladesh Supreme Court, High Court Division, is hereby directed to take necessary steps under section 161(2) of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984. 

End.
